According to the most trustworthy statistics the number of adult Dullards in the United States is but little short of thirty millions, including the statisticians. The intellectual centre of the race is somewhere about Peoria, Illinois, but the New England Dullard is the most shockingly moral.
revelationES: Necio consagrado es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: You assumed Dullard for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Aquello que severamente nos impele en dirección a la ganancia, siguiendo la línea del deseo.
biercEN: That which sternly impels us in the direction of profit, along the line of desire.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Deber probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: What you call Duty would probably be something else if you had to explain it without help.

biercES: Ejecutar sucesiva (y exitosamente) las funciones de masticación, humectación y deglución.
biercEN: To perform successively (and successfully) the functions of mastication, humectation, and deglutition.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Comer probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: You search for the meaning of Eat your whole life. Maybe the point is exactly not finding it.

biercES: Sorprender en secreto un catálogo de los crímenes y vicios de otro, o de uno mismo.
biercEN: Secretly to overhear a catalogue of the crimes and vices of another or yourself.
revelationES: Todos usan Escuchar a escondidas para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Eavesdrop is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Método de distinción tan barato que los necios lo emplean para acentuar su incapacidad.
biercEN: A method of distinction so cheap that fools employ it to accentuate their incapacity.
revelationES: Confundes la aprobación de Excentricidad con tener razón. No siempre coinciden.
revelationEN: Eccentricity changes villains every decade. The script is surprisingly the same.

biercES: Comprar el barril de whisky que no se necesita al precio de la vaca que no se puede pagar.
biercEN: Purchasing the barrel of whiskey that you do not need for the price of the cow that you cannot afford.
revelationES: Cuentas Economía que no tienes para imaginar la vida que no vas a vivir.
revelationEN: You work for Economy. Economy never works for you.

biercES: Bueno para comer y saludable de digerir, como un gusano para un sapo, un sapo para una serpiente, una serpiente para un cerdo, un cerdo para un hombre, y un hombre para un gusano.
biercEN: Good to eat, and wholesome to digest, as a worm to a toad, a toad to a snake, a snake to a pig, a pig to a man, and a man to a worm.
revelationES: Comestible es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: Edible looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Persona que combina las funciones judiciales de Minos, Radamantis y Éaco, pero que se aplaca con un óbolo; censor severamente virtuoso, pero tan caritativo que tolera las virtudes ajenas y los vicios propios; que arroja a su alrededor el rayo astillado y el trueno recio de la amonestación hasta parecerse a un manojo de petardos que expresa su opinión atado a la cola de un perro; y acto seguido murmura una tonada dulce y melodiosa, suave como el arrullo de un burro entonando su plegaria a la estrella vespertina.
biercEN: A person who combines the judicial functions of Minos, Rhadamanthus and Aeacus, but is placable with an obolus; a severely virtuous censor, but so charitable withal that he tolerates the virtues of others and the vices of himself; who flings about him the splintering lightning and sturdy thunders of admonition till he resembles a bunch of firecrackers petulantly uttering his mind at the tail of a dog; then straightway murmurs a mild, melodious lay, soft as the cooing of a donkey intoning its prayer to the evening star. Master of mysteries and lord of law, high-pinnacled upon the throne of thought, his face suffused with the dim splendors of the Transfiguration, his legs intertwisted and his tongue a-cheek, the editor spills his will along the paper and cuts it off in lengths to suit. And at intervals from behind the veil of the temple is heard the voice of the foreman demanding three inches of wit and six lines of religious meditation, or bidding him turn off the wisdom and whack up some pathos.
revelationES: Hablas de Editor como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: You talk about Editor as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Aquello que revela al sabio y disfraza ante el necio su falta de comprensión.
biercEN: That which discloses to the wise and disguises from the foolish their lack of understanding.
revelationES: Educación cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: You think you understand Education. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: El segundo de dos fenómenos que siempre ocurren juntos en el mismo orden. Al primero, llamado Causa, se dice que genera al otro, lo cual no es más sensato que si alguien que nunca vio un perro salvo persiguiendo un conejo declarara que el conejo es la causa del perro.
biercEN: The second of two phenomena which always occur together in the same order. The first, called a Cause, is said to generate the other--which is no more sensible than it would be for one who has never seen a dog except in the pursuit of a rabbit to declare the rabbit the cause of a dog.
revelationES: Todos usan Efecto para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Effect sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: Persona de mal gusto, más interesada en sí misma que en mí.
biercEN: A person of low taste, more interested in himself than in me.
revelationES: Buscas el sentido de Egoísta toda la vida. Puede que el punto sea justo no encontrarlo.
revelationEN: Egotist is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Remedio aprobado para la enfermedad de la locuacidad. También muy usado en casos de pobreza extrema.
biercEN: An approved remedy for the disease of garrulity. It is also much used in cases of extreme poverty.
revelationES: Hablas de Expulsión como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: You take Ejection for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: Aquel que goza del sagrado privilegio de votar por el candidato elegido por otro.
biercEN: One who enjoys the sacred privilege of voting for the man of another man's choice.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Elector probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: What you call Elector would probably be something else if you had to explain it without help.

biercES: El poder que causa todos los fenómenos naturales que no se sabe que estén causados por otra cosa. Es lo mismo que el rayo, y su célebre intento de fulminar al Dr. Franklin es uno de los episodios más pintorescos en la carrera de ese gran hombre de bien.
biercEN: The power that causes all natural phenomena not known to be caused by something else. It is the same thing as lightning, and its famous attempt to strike Dr. Franklin is one of the most picturesque incidents in that great and good man's career. The memory of Dr. Franklin is justly held in great reverence, particularly in France, where a waxen effigy of him was recently on exhibition, bearing the following touching account of his life and services to science:
revelationES: Le llamas normal a lo que Electricidad repite lo suficiente.
revelationEN: Nobody chose the rules of Electricity. Everyone defends them as if they had written them.

biercES: Composición en verso en la que, sin recurrir a método humorístico alguno, el autor procura producir en la mente del lector la más húmeda de las depresiones.
biercEN: A composition in verse, in which, without employing any of the methods of humor, the writer aims to produce in the reader's mind the dampest kind of dejection. The most famous English example begins somewhat like this:
revelationES: Hablas de Elegía como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: You search for the meaning of Elegy your whole life. Maybe the point is exactly not finding it.

biercES: El arte de persuadir oralmente a los necios de que el blanco es el color que parece ser. Incluye el don de hacer que cualquier color parezca blanco.
biercEN: The art of orally persuading fools that white is the color that it appears to be. It includes the gift of making any color appear white.
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Elocuencia con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: Eloquence feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: Imaginario país de delicias que los antiguos creían neciamente habitado por los espíritus de los buenos. Esta fábula ridícula y perniciosa fue barrida de la faz de la tierra por los primeros cristianos. ¡Que sus almas sean felices en el Cielo!
biercEN: An imaginary delightful country which the ancients foolishly believed to be inhabited by the spirits of the good. This ridiculous and mischievous fable was swept off the face of the earth by the early Christians--may their souls be happy in Heaven!
revelationES: Elíseo es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: You think you understand Elysium. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: El paso de un siervo de la tiranía ajena al despotismo propio.
biercEN: A bondman's change from the tyranny of another to the despotism of himself.
revelationES: Emancipación cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: You think you understand Emancipation. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Estafar a la vegetación encerrando los gases de los que se alimenta. Al embalsamar a sus muertos, y alterar así el equilibrio natural entre la vida animal y vegetal, los egipcios volvieron estéril e incapaz de sostener a más de una escasa población a su otrora fértil y poblado país.
biercEN: To cheat vegetation by locking up the gases upon which it feeds. By embalming their dead and thereby deranging the natural balance between animal and vegetable life, the Egyptians made their once fertile and populous country barren and incapable of supporting more than a meagre crew. The modern metallic burial casket is a step in the same direction, and many a dead man who ought now to be ornamenting his neighbor's lawn as a tree, or enriching his table as a bunch of radishes, is doomed to a long inutility. We shall get him after awhile if we are spared, but in the meantime the violet and rose are languishing for a nibble at his glutoeus maximus.
revelationES: Embalsamar perdona todo la primera vez. Cuenta cada vez después.
revelationEN: Embalm makes you promise things sanity would never sign off on.

biercES: Enfermedad postrante causada por una afluencia del corazón hacia la cabeza. A veces viene acompañada de una copiosa descarga de cloruro de sodio hidratado por los ojos.
biercEN: A prostrating disease caused by a determination of the heart to the head. It is sometimes accompanied by a copious discharge of hydrated chloride of sodium from the eyes.
revelationES: Te venden Emoción como meta. Nadie te dice que el podio está vacío cuando llegas.
revelationEN: You mistake Emotion for being busy. The clock does not tell the difference.

biercES: Especie particular (aunque no exquisita) de mentiroso.
biercEN: A special (but not particular) kind of liar.
revelationES: Panegirista es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: Encomiast sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: La posición más alejada, a cualquiera de los dos lados, del Interlocutor.
biercEN: The position farthest removed on either hand from the Interlocutor.
revelationES: Todos citan Final. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: End is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Todo lo que hay en el mundo, si te gusta.
biercEN: All there is in the world if you like it.
revelationES: Hablas de Suficiente como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: Enough is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Cualquier forma de diversión cuyos excesos se detienen antes de la muerte por inyección.
biercEN: Any kind of amusement whose inroads stop short of death by injection.
revelationES: Diste por sentado Entretenimiento durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: You name Entertainment and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Achaque de la juventud, curable con pequeñas dosis de arrepentimiento combinadas con aplicaciones externas de experiencia.
biercEN: A distemper of youth, curable by small doses of repentance in connection with outward applications of experience. Byron, who recovered long enough to call it "entuzy-muzy," had a relapse, which carried him off--to Missolonghi.
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Entusiasmo con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: Nobody tells you, but Enthusiasm is just the elegant way of accepting there is no answer.

biercES: El ataúd de un documento; la vaina de una factura; la cáscara de una remesa; el camisón de una carta de amor.
biercEN: The coffin of a document; the scabbard of a bill; the husk of a remittance; the bed-gown of a love-letter.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Sobre es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: You name Envelope and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Emulación adaptada a la capacidad más mezquina.
biercEN: Emulation adapted to the meanest capacity.
revelationES: Crees entender Envidia. La verdad es que nadie lo sabe, y actúan con tu misma confianza.
revelationEN: You think you understand Envy. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Insignia ornamentada que sirve para distinguir a un oficial militar del enemigo, es decir, del oficial de rango inferior a quien su muerte le daría el ascenso.
biercEN: An ornamented badge, serving to distinguish a military officer from the enemy--that is to say, from the officer of lower rank to whom his death would give promotion.
revelationES: Charretera cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Epaulet is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Un opositor de Epicuro, filósofo abstemio que, sosteniendo que el placer debía ser el fin principal del hombre, no perdía el tiempo en la gratificación de los sentidos.
biercEN: An opponent of Epicurus, an abstemious philosopher who, holding that pleasure should be the chief aim of man, wasted no time in gratification from the senses.
revelationES: Epicúreo es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: Epicure is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: Dicho breve y agudo, en prosa o en verso, frecuentemente caracterizado por la acidez o la acritud, y a veces por la sabiduría.
biercEN: A short, sharp saying in prose or verse, frequently characterized by acidity or acerbity and sometimes by wisdom. Following are some of the more notable epigrams of the learned and ingenious Dr. Jamrach Holobom:
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Epigrama con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: Epigram changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Inscripción en una tumba que demuestra que las virtudes adquiridas con la muerte tienen efecto retroactivo.
biercEN: An inscription on a tomb, showing that virtues acquired by death have a retroactive effect. Following is a touching example:
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Epitafio es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: Epitaph is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Polvo sacudido de un libro hacia un cráneo vacío.
biercEN: Dust shaken out of a book into an empty skull.
revelationES: Diste por sentado Erudición durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: Erudition looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Particularmente abstruso y consumadamente oculto. Las filosofías antiguas eran de dos clases: las exotéricas, que los propios filósofos podían entender en parte, y las esotéricas, que nadie podía entender. Son estas últimas las que más profundamente han influido en el pensamiento moderno.
biercEN: Very particularly abstruse and consummately occult. The ancient philosophies were of two kinds,--exoteric, those that the philosophers themselves could partly understand, and esoteric, those that nobody could understand. It is the latter that have most profoundly affected modern thought and found greatest acceptance in our time.
revelationES: Tu relación con Esotérico es la más larga y menos honesta que tendrás.
revelationEN: You work for Esoteric. Esoteric never works for you.

biercES: Ciencia que trata de las diversas tribus del Hombre, a saber: bandidos, ladrones, estafadores, tontos, dementes, idiotas y etnólogos.
biercEN: The science that treats of the various tribes of Man, as robbers, thieves, swindlers, dunces, lunatics, idiots and ethnologists.
revelationES: Etnología es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: Ethnology feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: Banquete sagrado de la secta religiosa de los Teófagos. Una disputa surgió lamentablemente entre los miembros de esta secta acerca de qué era exactamente lo que comían. En esta controversia han muerto ya unos quinientos mil, y la cuestión sigue sin resolverse.
biercEN: A sacred feast of the religious sect of Theophagi. A dispute once unhappily arose among the members of this sect as to what it was that they ate. In this controversy some five hundred thousand have already been slain, and the question is still unsettled.
revelationES: Diste por sentado Eucaristía durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: Eucharist is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Alabanza de una persona que tiene las ventajas de la riqueza y el poder, o la consideración de estar muerta.
biercEN: Praise of a person who has either the advantages of wealth and power, or the consideration to be dead.
revelationES: Elogio fúnebre te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: Eulogy sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: Portador de buenas nuevas, particularmente (en sentido religioso) de aquellas que nos aseguran nuestra propia salvación y la condenación del prójimo.
biercEN: A bearer of good tidings, particularly (in a religious sense) such as assure us of our own salvation and the damnation of our neighbors.
revelationES: Evangelista es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: You call Evangelist the habit of never questioning anything deeper.

biercES: Que dura para siempre. No sin cierta timidez me atrevo a ofrecer esta breve y elemental definición, pues no ignoro la existencia de un voluminoso tratado, en otro tiempo tenido por gran autoridad, dedicado enteramente a explicar esta sola palabra.
biercEN: Lasting forever. It is with no small diffidence that I venture to offer this brief and elementary definition, for I am not unaware of the existence of a bulky volume by a sometime Bishop of Worcester, entitled, A Partial Definition of the Word "Everlasting," as Used in the Authorized Version of the Holy Scriptures. His book was once esteemed of great authority in the Anglican Church, and is still, I understand, studied with pleasure to the mind and profit of the soul.
revelationES: Eterno parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: You assumed Everlasting for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Cosa que se toma la libertad de diferir de las demás de su clase, como un hombre honesto, una mujer sincera, etcétera. 'La excepción confirma la regla' es una frase constantemente repetida por los ignorantes, que la reproducen unos de otros sin pensar jamás en su absurdo. En latín, Exceptio probat regulam significa que la excepción pone a prueba la regla, no que la confirma.
biercEN: A thing which takes the liberty to differ from other things of its class, as an honest man, a truthful woman, etc. "The exception proves the rule" is an expression constantly upon the lips of the ignorant, who parrot it from one another with never a thought of its absurdity. In the Latin, "Exceptio probat regulam" means that the exception tests the rule, puts it to the proof, not confirms it. The malefactor who drew the meaning from this excellent dictum and substituted a contrary one of his own exerted an evil power which appears to be immortal.
revelationES: Buscas el sentido de Excepción toda la vida. Puede que el punto sea justo no encontrarlo.
revelationEN: Exception feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: En moral, indulgencia que impone, mediante castigos apropiados, la ley de la moderación.
biercEN: In morals, an indulgence that enforces by appropriate penalties the law of moderation.
revelationES: Hablas de Exceso como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: Excess sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: Funcionario del Gobierno cuyo deber es hacer cumplir la voluntad del poder legislativo, hasta que el poder judicial tenga a bien declararla inválida y sin efecto.
biercEN: An officer of the Government, whose duty it is to enforce the wishes of the legislative power until such time as the judicial department shall be pleased to pronounce them invalid and of no effect. Following is an extract from an old book entitled, The Lunarian Astonished--Pfeiffer & Co., Boston, 1803:
revelationES: Poder Ejecutivo se ejerce mejor cuando nadie nota que lo estás ejerciendo.
revelationEN: Executive corrupts. The interesting part is how fast you find the excuse.

biercES: En materia religiosa, ensartar la conciencia ajena en un asador y tostarla hasta dejarla en un incómodo tono castaño.
biercEN: In religious affairs, to put the conscience of another upon the spit and roast it to a nut-brown discomfort.
revelationES: Exhortar cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Exhort is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Aquel que sirve a su patria residiendo en el extranjero, sin ser por ello embajador.
biercEN: One who serves his country by residing abroad, yet is not an ambassador.
revelationES: Exiliado cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: You take Exile for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: La sabiduría que nos permite reconocer como una desagradable vieja conocida a la necedad que ya hemos abrazado antes.
biercEN: The wisdom that enables us to recognize as an undesirable old acquaintance the folly that we have already embraced.
revelationES: Experiencia es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Experience to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: Uno de los muchos métodos por los cuales los necios prefieren perder a sus amigos.
biercEN: One of the many methods by which fools prefer to lose their friends.
revelationES: Reconvención suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Expostulation is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: La materia prima con la que la teología creó el estado futuro.
biercEN: The raw material out of which theology created the future state.
revelationES: Damos por hecho Extinción hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: You talk about Extinction as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Criatura de forma y dotes variadas, que antiguamente habitaba prados y bosques. Era de hábitos nocturnos, y algo aficionada al baile y al robo de niños. Los naturalistas creen hoy que las hadas están extintas, aunque un clérigo de la Iglesia de Inglaterra vio tres cerca de Colchester tan tarde como en 1855, al atravesar un parque tras cenar con el señor de la mansión.
biercEN: A creature, variously fashioned and endowed, that formerly inhabited the meadows and forests. It was nocturnal in its habits, and somewhat addicted to dancing and the theft of children. The fairies are now believed by naturalists to be extinct, though a clergyman of the Church of England saw three near Colchester as lately as 1855, while passing through a park after dining with the lord of the manor. The sight greatly staggered him, and he was so affected that his account of it was incoherent. In the year 1807 a troop of fairies visited a wood near Aix and carried off the daughter of a peasant, who had been seen to enter it with a bundle of clothing. The son of a wealthy bourgeois disappeared about the same time, but afterward returned. He had seen the abduction and been in pursuit of the fairies. Justinian Gaux, a writer of the fourteenth century, avers that so great is the fairies' power of transformation that he saw one change itself into two opposing armies and fight a battle with great slaughter, and that the next day, after it had resumed its original shape and gone away, there were seven hundred bodies of the slain which the villagers had to bury. He does not say if any of the wounded recovered. In the time of Henry III, of England, a law was made which prescribed the death penalty for "Kyllynge, wowndynge, or mamynge" a fairy, and it was universally respected.
revelationES: Diste por sentado Hada durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: Nobody tells you, but Fairy is just the elegant way of accepting there is no answer.

biercES: Creencia sin pruebas en lo que dice quien habla sin conocimiento, de cosas sin parangón.
biercEN: Belief without evidence in what is told by one who speaks without knowledge, of things without parallel.
revelationES: Fe es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: What you call Faith would probably be something else if you had to explain it without help.

biercES: Notoriamente desdichado.
biercEN: Conspicuously miserable.
revelationES: Famoso cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Famous is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Un déspota al que los sabios ridiculizan y obedecen.
biercEN: A despot whom the wise ridicule and obey.
revelationES: Moda es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: You mistake having an opinion about Fashion for having understood it.

biercES: Un festejo. Celebración religiosa que suele señalarse por la gula y la embriaguez, con frecuencia en honor de alguna persona santa distinguida por su abstinencia.
biercEN: A festival. A religious celebration usually signalized by gluttony and drunkenness, frequently in honor of some holy person distinguished for abstemiousness. In the Roman Catholic Church feasts are "movable" and "immovable," but the celebrants are uniformly immovable until they are full. In their earliest development these entertainments took the form of feasts for the dead; such were held by the Greeks, under the name Nemeseia, by the Aztecs and Peruvians, as in modern times they are popular with the Chinese; though it is believed that the ancient dead, like the modern, were light eaters. Among the many feasts of the Romans was the Novemdiale, which was held, according to Livy, whenever stones fell from heaven.
revelationES: Festín suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Feast is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Persona de mayor iniciativa que discreción, que al aprovechar una oportunidad ha formado un apego desafortunado.
biercEN: A person of greater enterprise than discretion, who in embracing an opportunity has formed an unfortunate attachment.
revelationES: Delincuente es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: You name Felon and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Miembro del sexo opuesto, o desleal.
biercEN: One of the opposing, or unfair, sex.
revelationES: Mujer es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: You mistake having an opinion about Female for having understood it.

biercES: Una mentira que aún no ha echado los dientes. El acercamiento más cercano a la verdad que logra un mentiroso habitual: el perigeo de su órbita excéntrica.
biercEN: A lie that has not cut its teeth. An habitual liar's nearest approach to truth: the perigee of his eccentric orbit.
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Mentirijilla con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: You take Fib for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: La reiterada saciedad de un afecto emprendedor.
biercEN: The iterated satiety of an enterprising affection.
revelationES: Inconstancia es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: Fickleness is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: Instrumento para hacerle cosquillas al oído humano mediante la fricción de la cola de un caballo contra las entrañas de un gato.
biercEN: An instrument to tickle human ears by friction of a horse's tail on the entrails of a cat.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Violín es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: Fiddle is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Virtud peculiar de quienes están a punto de ser traicionados.
biercEN: A virtue peculiar to those who are about to be betrayed.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Fidelidad probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: You assumed Fidelity for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: El arte o ciencia de administrar rentas y recursos para el mayor beneficio del administrador.
biercEN: The art or science of managing revenues and resources for the best advantage of the manager. The pronunciation of this word with the i long and the accent on the first syllable is one of America's most precious discoveries and possessions.
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Finanzas con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: You assumed Finance for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Trapo de color que se enarbola sobre las tropas y se iza en fuertes y buques. Parece cumplir la misma función que ciertos carteles que se ven en terrenos baldíos: 'Aquí se puede tirar la basura.'
biercEN: A colored rag borne above troops and hoisted on forts and ships. It appears to serve the same purpose as certain signs that one sees on vacant lots in London--"Rubbish may be shot here."
revelationES: Bandera es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: You think you understand Flag. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: La Segunda Persona de la Trinidad secular.
biercEN: The Second Person of the secular Trinity.
revelationES: Carne es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: You think you understand Flesh. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Cambiar súbitamente de opinión y pasarse a otro partido. El caso más notable registrado es el de Saulo de Tarso, severamente criticado como tránsfuga por ciertos diarios partidistas de nuestros días.
biercEN: Suddenly to change one's opinions and go over to another party. The most notable flop on record was that of Saul of Tarsus, who has been severely criticised as a turn-coat by some of our partisan journals.
revelationES: Voltear casaca cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Flop is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: El prototipo de la puntuación. Se ha observado que los sistemas de puntuación empleados por las diversas naciones literarias dependieron originalmente de los hábitos sociales y la dieta general de las moscas que infestaban cada país.
biercEN: The prototype of punctuation. It is observed by Garvinus that the systems of punctuation in use by the various literary nations depended originally upon the social habits and general diet of the flies infesting the several countries. These creatures, which have always been distinguished for a neighborly and companionable familiarity with authors, liberally or niggardly embellish the manuscripts in process of growth under the pen, according to their bodily habit, bringing out the sense of the work by a species of interpretation superior to, and independent of, the writer's powers. The "old masters" of literature--that is to say, the early writers whose work is so esteemed by later scribes and critics in the same language--never punctuated at all, but worked right along free-handed, without that abruption of the thought which comes from the use of points. (We observe the same thing in children to-day, whose usage in this particular is a striking and beautiful instance of the law that the infancy of individuals reproduces the methods and stages of development characterizing the infancy of races.) In the work of these primitive scribes all the punctuation is found, by the modern investigator with his optical instruments and chemical tests, to have been inserted by the writers' ingenious and serviceable collaborator, the common house-fly--Musca maledicta. In transcribing these ancient MSS, for the purpose of either making the work their own or preserving what they naturally regard as divine revelations, later writers reverently and accurately copy whatever marks they find upon the papyrus or parchment, to the unspeakable enhancement of the lucidity of the thought and value of the work. Writers contemporary with the copyists naturally avail themselves of the obvious advantages of these marks in their own work, and with such assistance as the flies of their own household may be willing to grant, frequently rival and sometimes surpass the older compositions, in respect at least of punctuation, which is no small glory. Fully to understand the important services that flies perform to literature it is only necessary to lay a page of some popular novelist alongside a saucer of cream-and-molasses in a sunny room and observe "how the wit brightens and the style refines" in accurate proportion to the duration of exposure.
revelationES: Todos citan Mancha de mosca. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: You assumed Fly-Speck for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Ese 'don y facultad divina' cuya energía creadora y directriz inspira la mente del Hombre, guía sus acciones y adorna su vida.
biercEN: That "gift and faculty divine" whose creative and controlling energy inspires Man's mind, guides his actions and adorns his life.
revelationES: Locura es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: You think you understand Folly. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Persona que permea el dominio de la especulación intelectual y se difunde por los canales de la actividad moral. Es omnífico, omniforme, omnipercipiente, omnisciente, omnipotente. Fue él quien inventó las letras, la imprenta, el ferrocarril, el barco de vapor, el telégrafo, la perogrullada y el círculo de las ciencias.
biercEN: A person who pervades the domain of intellectual speculation and diffuses himself through the channels of moral activity. He is omnific, omniform, omnipercipient, omniscient, omnipotent. He it was who invented letters, printing, the railroad, the steamboat, the telegraph, the platitude and the circle of the sciences. He created patriotism and taught the nations war--founded theology, philosophy, law, medicine and Chicago. He established monarchical and republican government. He is from everlasting to everlasting--such as creation's dawn beheld he fooleth now. In the morning of time he sang upon primitive hills, and in the noonday of existence headed the procession of being. His grandmotherly hand was warmly tucked-in the set sun of civilization, and in the twilight he prepares Man's evening meal of milk-and-morality and turns down the covers of the universal grave. And after the rest of us shall have retired for the night of eternal oblivion he will sit up to write a history of human civilization.
revelationES: Le llamas Necio a la costumbre de no cuestionar nada más profundo.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Fool. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: El dedo comúnmente usado para señalar a dos malhechores.
biercEN: The finger commonly used in pointing out two malefactors.
revelationES: Crees entender Dedo índice. La verdad es que nadie lo sabe, y actúan con tu misma confianza.
revelationEN: You talk about Forefinger as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Parece una palabra fácil de definir, pero cuando considero que píos y eruditos teólogos han pasado largas vidas explicándola, y escrito bibliotecas para explicar sus explicaciones, me quedo pasmado ante el imponente problema de su significado, y remito humildemente la cuestión a autoridades más eminentes que yo.
biercEN: This looks like an easy word to define, but when I consider that pious and learned theologians have spent long lives in explaining it, and written libraries to explain their explanations; when I remember that nations have been divided and bloody battles caused by the difference between foreordination and predestination, and that millions of treasure have been expended in the effort to prove and disprove its compatibility with freedom of the will and the efficacy of prayer, praise, and a religious life,--recalling these awful facts in the history of the word, I stand appalled before the mighty problem of its signification, abase my spiritual eyes, fearing to contemplate its portentous magnitude, reverently uncover and humbly refer it to His Eminence Cardinal Gibbons and His Grace Bishop Potter.
revelationES: Confundes la aprobación de Preordinación con tener razón. No siempre coinciden.
revelationEN: You think you decide for yourself. Foreordination just let you pick from its options.

biercES: Don de Dios otorgado a los médicos en compensación por su carencia de conciencia.
biercEN: A gift of God bestowed upon doctors in compensation for their destitution of conscience.
revelationES: Olvido es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: Forgetfulness feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: Instrumento usado principalmente para introducir animales muertos en la boca. Antiguamente se empleaba el cuchillo con este fin, y muchas personas dignas todavía lo consideran superior al otro utensilio, aunque no lo rechazan del todo, sino que lo usan como ayuda para cargar el cuchillo.
biercEN: An instrument used chiefly for the purpose of putting dead animals into the mouth. Formerly the knife was employed for this purpose, and by many worthy persons is still thought to have many advantages over the other tool, which, however, they do not altogether reject, but use to assist in charging the knife. The immunity of these persons from swift and awful death is one of the most striking proofs of God's mercy to those that hate Him.
revelationES: Tenedor te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: What you call Fork would probably be something else if you had to explain it without help.

biercES: Régimen por el cual una corporación religiosa retiene tierras a condición de rezar por el alma del donante. En la Edad Media, muchas de las hermandades más ricas obtuvieron así sus propiedades, de manera simple y económica.
biercEN: The tenure by which a religious corporation holds lands on condition of praying for the soul of the donor. In mediaeval times many of the wealthiest fraternities obtained their estates in this simple and cheap manner, and once when Henry VIII of England sent an officer to confiscate certain vast possessions which a fraternity of monks held by frankalmoigne, "What!" said the Prior, "would your master stay our benefactor's soul in Purgatory?" "Ay," said the officer, coldly, "an ye will not pray him thence for naught he must e'en roast." "But look you, my son," persisted the good man, "this act hath rank as robbery of God!" "Nay, nay, good father, my master the king doth but deliver Him from the manifold temptations of too great wealth."
revelationES: Todos usan Tenencia eclesiástica gratuita para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: You name Frankalmoigne and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Conquistador a pequeña escala, cuyas anexiones carecen del mérito santificador de la magnitud.
biercEN: A conqueror in a small way of business, whose annexations lack of the sanctifying merit of magnitude.
revelationES: Todos usan Filibustero para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Freebooter is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Exención del peso de la autoridad en una mísera media docena de los infinitos métodos de la coerción. Condición política que toda nación supone disfrutar en virtual monopolio.
biercEN: Exemption from the stress of authority in a beggarly half dozen of restraint's infinite multitude of methods. A political condition that every nation supposes itself to enjoy in virtual monopoly. Liberty. The distinction between freedom and liberty is not accurately known; naturalists have never been able to find a living specimen of either.
revelationES: Libertad cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Freedom. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: Orden con ritos secretos, ceremonias grotescas y disfraces fantásticos que, originada en el reinado de Carlos II entre artesanos londinenses, ha sido sucesivamente adoptada por los muertos de siglos pasados en ininterrumpida retrogresión, hasta abarcar hoy a todas las generaciones humanas anteriores a Adán.
biercEN: An order with secret rites, grotesque ceremonies and fantastic costumes, which, originating in the reign of Charles II, among working artisans of London, has been joined successively by the dead of past centuries in unbroken retrogression until now it embraces all the generations of man on the hither side of Adam and is drumming up distinguished recruits among the pre-Creational inhabitants of Chaos and Formless Void. The order was founded at different times by Charlemagne, Julius Caesar, Cyrus, Solomon, Zoroaster, Confucious, Thothmes, and Buddha. Its emblems and symbols have been found in the Catacombs of Paris and Rome, on the stones of the Parthenon and the Chinese Great Wall, among the temples of Karnak and Palmyra and in the Egyptian Pyramids--always by a Freemason.
revelationES: Masones dura mientras a ambos les conviene fingir que dura por otra razón.
revelationEN: You mistake Freemasons for having someone nearby. They are not always the same thing.

biercES: Que no tiene favores que otorgar. Desprovisto de fortuna. Aficionado a proferir la verdad y el sentido común.
biercEN: Having no favors to bestow. Destitute of fortune. Addicted to utterance of truth and common sense.
revelationES: Sin amigos dura mientras a ambos les conviene fingir que dura por otra razón.
revelationEN: You mistake Friendless for having someone nearby. They are not always the same thing.

biercES: Un barco lo bastante grande como para llevar a dos personas con buen tiempo, pero solo a una con mal tiempo.
biercEN: A ship big enough to carry two in fair weather, but only one in foul.
revelationES: Nadie te avisa que Amistad también se termina por aburrimiento, no solo por traición.
revelationEN: Friendship survives distance, almost never comfort.

biercES: Reptil de patas comestibles. La primera mención de las ranas en la literatura profana aparece en el relato homérico de la guerra entre ellas y los ratones. La rana es una cantante diligente, de buena voz pero sin oído.
biercEN: A reptile with edible legs. The first mention of frogs in profane literature is in Homer's narrative of the war between them and the mice. Skeptical persons have doubted Homer's authorship of the work, but the learned, ingenious and industrious Dr. Schliemann has set the question forever at rest by uncovering the bones of the slain frogs. One of the forms of moral suasion by which Pharaoh was besought to favor the Israelities was a plague of frogs, but Pharaoh, who liked them fricasees, remarked, with truly oriental stoicism, that he could stand it as long as the frogs and the Jews could; so the programme was changed. The frog is a diligent songster, having a good voice but no ear. The libretto of his favorite opera, as written by Aristophanes, is brief, simple and effective--"brekekex-koax"; the music is apparently by that eminent composer, Richard Wagner. Horses have a frog in each hoof--a thoughtful provision of nature, enabling them to shine in a hurdle race.
revelationES: Diste por sentado Rana durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: You think you understand Frog. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Parte del aparato penal empleado en esa institución punitiva que es la cocina de una mujer. La sartén fue inventada por Calvino, quien la usaba para cocinar bebés que habían muerto sin bautismo.
biercEN: One part of the penal apparatus employed in that punitive institution, a woman's kitchen. The frying-pan was invented by Calvin, and by him used in cooking span-long infants that had died without baptism; and observing one day the horrible torment of a tramp who had incautiously pulled a fried babe from the waste-dump and devoured it, it occurred to the great divine to rob death of its terrors by introducing the frying-pan into every household in Geneva. Thence it spread to all corners of the world, and has been of invaluable assistance in the propagation of his sombre faith. The following lines (said to be from the pen of his Grace Bishop Potter) seem to imply that the usefulness of this utensil is not limited to this world; but as the consequences of its employment in this life reach over into the life to come, so also itself may be found on the other side, rewarding its devotees:
revelationES: Sartén cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: You talk about Frying-Pan as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Espectáculo con el que demostramos nuestro respeto por el muerto enriqueciendo al sepulturero, y fortalecemos nuestro duelo con un gasto que profundiza nuestros gemidos y duplica nuestras lágrimas.
biercEN: A pageant whereby we attest our respect for the dead by enriching the undertaker, and strengthen our grief by an expenditure that deepens our groans and doubles our tears.
revelationES: Funeral es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: Funeral is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: Ese período de tiempo en que nuestros asuntos prosperan, nuestros amigos son leales y nuestra felicidad está asegurada.
biercEN: That period of time in which our affairs prosper, our friends are true and our happiness is assured.
revelationES: Hablas de Futuro como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: Future is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Escenario para la representación de autos sacramentales, en el que el actor principal es trasladado al cielo. En este país, la horca es notable sobre todo por la cantidad de personas que logran escapar de ella.
biercEN: A stage for the performance of miracle plays, in which the leading actor is translated to heaven. In this country the gallows is chiefly remarkable for the number of persons who escape it.
revelationES: Horca cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Gallows changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Canaleta pluvial que sobresale del alero de los edificios medievales, comúnmente esculpida como caricatura grotesca de algún enemigo personal del arquitecto o del dueño del edificio.
biercEN: A rain-spout projecting from the eaves of mediaeval buildings, commonly fashioned into a grotesque caricature of some personal enemy of the architect or owner of the building. This was especially the case in churches and ecclesiastical structures generally, in which the gargoyles presented a perfect rogues' gallery of local heretics and controversialists. Sometimes when a new dean and chapter were installed the old gargoyles were removed and others substituted having a closer relation to the private animosities of the new incumbents.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Gárgola es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: You assumed Gargoyle for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Banda elástica destinada a impedir que una mujer se salga de sus medias y asuele el país.
biercEN: An elastic band intended to keep a woman from coming out of her stockings and desolating the country.
revelationES: Liguero es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: Garther looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Originalmente esta palabra significaba noble de nacimiento, y se aplicaba con justicia a una gran multitud de personas. Hoy significa noble de espíritu, y se toma un descanso.
biercEN: Originally this word meant noble by birth and was rightly applied to a great multitude of persons. It now means noble by nature and is taking a bit of a rest.
revelationES: Todos usan Generoso para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Generous is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Relato de la descendencia de uno a partir de un antepasado a quien no le interesaba particularmente rastrear la suya propia.
biercEN: An account of one's descent from an ancestor who did not particularly care to trace his own.
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Genealogía con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: Genealogy sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: Refinado, a la manera de un dandi.
biercEN: Refined, after the fashion of a gent.
revelationES: Le llamas normal a lo que Elegante repite lo suficiente.
revelationEN: Genteel demands authenticity, as long as it looks like everyone else’s.

biercES: Sujeto capaz de explicarte al instante la diferencia entre el exterior del mundo y su interior.
biercEN: A chap who can tell you offhand the difference between the outside of the world and the inside.
revelationES: Todos citan Geógrafo. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: You assumed Geographer for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Ciencia de la corteza terrestre, a la que sin duda se sumará la de su interior el día en que un hombre salga parlanchín de un pozo.
biercEN: The science of the earth's crust--to which, doubtless, will be added that of its interior whenever a man shall come up garrulous out of a well. The geological formations of the globe already noted are catalogued thus: The Primary, or lower one, consists of rocks, bones or mired mules, gas-pipes, miners' tools, antique statues minus the nose, Spanish doubloons and ancestors. The Secondary is largely made up of red worms and moles. The Tertiary comprises railway tracks, patent pavements, grass, snakes, mouldy boots, beer bottles, tomato cans, intoxicated citizens, garbage, anarchists, snap-dogs and fools.
revelationES: Damos por hecho Geología hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Geology. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: El signo externo y visible de un miedo interno.
biercEN: The outward and visible sign of an inward fear.
revelationES: Nadie te avisa que Fantasma también se termina por aburrimiento, no solo por traición.
revelationEN: Nobody warns you Ghost also ends from boredom, not only from betrayal.

biercES: Demonio adicto al reprensible hábito de devorar a los muertos. Su existencia ha sido disputada por esa clase de polemistas más empeñados en privar al mundo de creencias reconfortantes que en ofrecerle algo mejor en su lugar.
biercEN: A demon addicted to the reprehensible habit of devouring the dead. The existence of ghouls has been disputed by that class of controversialists who are more concerned to deprive the world of comforting beliefs than to give it anything good in their place. In 1640 Father Secchi saw one in a cemetery near Florence and frightened it away with the sign of the cross. He describes it as gifted with many heads and an uncommon allowance of limbs, and he saw it in more than one place at a time. The good man was coming away from dinner at the time and explains that if he had not been "heavy with eating" he would have seized the demon at all hazards. Atholston relates that a ghoul was caught by some sturdy peasants in a churchyard at Sudbury and ducked in a horsepond. (He appears to think that so distinguished a criminal should have been ducked in a tank of rosewater.) The water turned at once to blood "and so contynues unto ys daye." The pond has since been bled with a ditch. As late as the beginning of the fourteenth century a ghoul was cornered in the crypt of the cathedral at Amiens and the whole population surrounded the place. Twenty armed men with a priest at their head, bearing a crucifix, entered and captured the ghoul, which, thinking to escape by the stratagem, had transformed itself to the semblance of a well known citizen, but was nevertheless hanged, drawn and quartered in the midst of hideous popular orgies. The citizen whose shape the demon had assumed was so affected by the sinister occurrence that he never again showed himself in Amiens and his fate remains a mystery.
revelationES: Buscas el sentido de Necrófago toda la vida. Puede que el punto sea justo no encontrarlo.
revelationEN: Ghoul looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Persona que escapa de los males de la moderación cometiendo dispepsia.
biercEN: A person who escapes the evils of moderation by committing dyspepsia.
revelationES: Glotón suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Glutton feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: En la mitología del norte de Europa, duende enano que habita las entrañas de la tierra y custodia especialmente los tesoros minerales.
biercEN: In North-European mythology, a dwarfish imp inhabiting the interior parts of the earth and having special custody of mineral treasures. Bjorsen, who died in 1765, says gnomes were common enough in the southern parts of Sweden in his boyhood, and he frequently saw them scampering on the hills in the evening twilight. Ludwig Binkerhoof saw three as recently as 1792, in the Black Forest, and Sneddeker avers that in 1803 they drove a party of miners out of a Silesian mine. Basing our computations upon data supplied by these statements, we find that the gnomes were probably extinct as early as 1764.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Gnomo probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: You search for the meaning of Gnome your whole life. Maybe the point is exactly not finding it.

biercES: Secta de filósofos que intentaron fraguar una fusión entre los primeros cristianos y los platónicos. Los primeros no quisieron sumarse a la mesa de negociación, y la fusión fracasó, para gran disgusto de sus gestores.
biercEN: A sect of philosophers who tried to engineer a fusion between the early Christians and the Platonists. The former would not go into the caucus and the combination failed, greatly to the chagrin of the fusion managers.
revelationES: Gnósticos es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: Gnostics is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Animal de Sudáfrica que, domesticado, se parece a un caballo, un búfalo y un ciervo. En estado salvaje, se parece más bien a un rayo, un terremoto y un ciclón.
biercEN: An animal of South Africa, which in its domesticated state resembles a horse, a buffalo and a stag. In its wild condition it is something like a thunderbolt, an earthquake and a cyclone.
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Ñu con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Gnu to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: Sensata, señora, respecto del valor del presente escritor. Advertido, señor, de las ventajas de dejarlo tranquilo.
biercEN: Sensible, madam, to the worth of this present writer. Alive, sir, to the advantages of letting him alone.

biercES: Bomba muscular automática de sangre. En sentido figurado, se dice que este útil órgano es la sede de las emociones y los sentimientos: una fantasía muy bonita que, sin embargo, no es más que la supervivencia de una creencia antaño universal. Hoy se sabe que los sentimientos y las emociones residen en el estómago.
biercEN: An automatic, muscular blood-pump. Figuratively, this useful organ is said to be the seat of emotions and sentiments--a very pretty fancy which, however, is nothing but a survival of a once universal belief. It is now known that the sentiments and emotions reside in the stomach, being evolved from food by chemical action of the gastric fluid. The exact process by which a beefsteak becomes a feeling--tender or not, according to the age of the animal from which it was cut; the successive stages of elaboration through which a caviar sandwich is transmuted to a quaint fancy and reappears as a pungent epigram; the marvelous functional methods of converting a hard-boiled egg into religious contrition, or a cream-puff into a sigh of sensibility--these things have been patiently ascertained by M. Pasteur, and by him expounded with convincing lucidity. (See, also, my monograph, The Essential Identity of the Spiritual Affections and Certain Intestinal Gases Freed in Digestion--4to, 687 pp.) In a scientific work entitled, I believe, Delectatio Demonorum (John Camden Hotton, London, 1873) this view of the sentiments receives a striking illustration; and for further light consult Professor Dam's famous treatise on Love as a Product of Alimentary Maceration.

biercEN: To pass the winter season in domestic seclusion. There have been many singular popular notions about the hibernation of various animals. Many believe that the bear hibernates during the whole winter and subsists by mechanically sucking its paws. It is admitted that it comes out of its retirement in the spring so lean that it had to try twice before it can cast a shadow. Three or four centuries ago, in England, no fact was better attested than that swallows passed the winter months in the mud at the bottom of their brooks, clinging together in globular masses. They have apparently been compelled to give up the custom on account of the foulness of the brooks. Sotus Ecobius discovered in Central Asia a whole nation of people who hibernate. By some investigators, the fasting of Lent is supposed to have been originally a modified form of hibernation, to which the Church gave a religious significance; but this view was strenuously opposed by that eminent authority, Bishop Kip, who did not wish any honors denied to the memory of the Founder of his family.
