House-maid, a youngerly person of the opposing sex employed to be variously disagreeable and ingeniously unclean in the station in which it has pleased God to place her.
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Casa con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: You mistake having an opinion about House for having understood it.

biercES: Que ha pagado todos los impuestos sobre bienes del hogar.
biercEN: Having paid all taxes on household goods.
revelationES: Sin techo suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Nobody tells you, but Houseless is just the elegant way of accepting there is no answer.

biercES: El fruto de una flor llamada Palacio.
biercEN: The fruit of a flower called the Palace.
revelationES: Choza parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Hovel. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: La raza humana, colectivamente, con exclusión de los poetas antropoides.
biercEN: The human race, collectively, exclusive of the anthropoid poets.
revelationES: Damos por hecho Humanidad hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: Humanity looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Plaga que habría ablandado la austeridad canosa del corazón del Faraón, y lo habría persuadido de despedir a Israel con sus mejores deseos, en un santiamén.
biercEN: A plague that would have softened down the hoar austerity of Pharaoh's heart and persuaded him to dismiss Israel with his best wishes, cat-quick.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Humorista probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: You take Humorist for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: Fenómeno atmosférico antaño muy común, hoy generalmente reemplazado por el tornado y el ciclón. El huracán sigue en uso popular en las Antillas, y lo prefieren ciertos capitanes de mar de la vieja escuela.
biercEN: An atmospheric demonstration once very common but now generally abandoned for the tornado and cyclone. The hurricane is still in popular use in the West Indies and is preferred by certain old-fashioned sea-captains. It is also used in the construction of the upper decks of steamboats, but generally speaking, the hurricane's usefulness has outlasted it.
revelationES: Buscas el sentido de Huracán toda la vida. Puede que el punto sea justo no encontrarlo.
revelationEN: Hurricane changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: El despacho de los chapuceros.
biercEN: The dispatch of bunglers.
revelationES: Apuro es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: You think you understand Hurry. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Aquel que, tras haber cenado, queda a cargo de cuidar la vajilla.
biercEN: One who, having dined, is charged with the care of the plate.
revelationES: Buscas Marido verdadero. Aceptas el que aparece cuando estás cansado de buscar.
revelationEN: Nobody told you Husband is billed in silences too, not only in kisses.

biercES: Un asunto puesto en común.
biercEN: A pooled issue.
revelationES: Híbrido es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: You name Hybrid and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Especie de animal que los antiguos catalogaban por muchas cabezas.
biercEN: A kind of animal that the ancients catalogued under many heads.
revelationES: Todos usan Hidra para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: You call Hydra the habit of never questioning anything deeper.

biercES: Bestia venerada por algunas naciones orientales por su costumbre de frecuentar de noche los cementerios. Pero el estudiante de medicina hace lo mismo.
biercEN: A beast held in reverence by some oriental nations from its habit of frequenting at night the burial-places of the dead. But the medical student does that.
revelationES: Hiena es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: Hyena is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: Depresión del ánimo propio.
biercEN: Depression of one's own spirits.
revelationES: Hipocondría es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: Hypochondriasis is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Aquel que, profesando virtudes que no respeta, obtiene la ventaja de parecer aquello que desprecia.
biercEN: One who, professing virtues that he does not respect secures the advantage of seeming to be what he despises.
revelationES: Hipócrita es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: Hypocrite is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Fluido que hace las veces de sangre para dioses y diosas.
biercEN: A fluid that serves the gods and goddesses in place of blood.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Icor es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: Ichor looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Destructor de ídolos, cuyos adoradores quedan imperfectamente satisfechos con la faena, y protestan enérgicamente que este derriba pero no reedifica, que derrumba pero no apila.
biercEN: A breaker of idols, the worshipers whereof are imperfectly gratified by the performance, and most strenuously protest that he unbuildeth but doth not reedify, that he pulleth down but pileth not up. For the poor things would have other idols in place of those he thwacketh upon the mazzard and dispelleth. But the iconoclast saith: "Ye shall have none at all, for ye need them not; and if the rebuilder fooleth round hereabout, behold I will depress the head of him and sit thereon till he squawk it."
revelationES: Todos citan Iconoclasta. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: Iconoclast is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Miembro de una tribu vasta y poderosa cuya influencia en los asuntos humanos ha sido siempre dominante y determinante. La actividad del Idiota no se limita a ningún campo especial del pensamiento o la acción, sino que 'lo permea y regula todo'. Tiene siempre la última palabra en todo; su decisión es inapelable.
biercEN: A member of a large and powerful tribe whose influence in human affairs has always been dominant and controlling. The Idiot's activity is not confined to any special field of thought or action, but "pervades and regulates the whole." He has the last word in everything; his decision is unappealable. He sets the fashions and opinion of taste, dictates the limitations of speech and circumscribes conduct with a dead-line.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Idiota probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: Idiot is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Granja modelo donde el diablo experimenta con semillas de nuevos pecados y promueve el cultivo de vicios básicos.
biercEN: A model farm where the devil experiments with seeds of new sins and promotes the growth of staple vices.
revelationES: Todos hablan de Ociosidad en el currículum. Nadie lo pone en la lápida.
revelationEN: You chase Idleness your whole life. The moment you get it, you already want something else.

biercES: Persona no familiarizada con ciertas clases de conocimiento que a uno le resultan familiares, y que posee ciertas otras clases de las que uno no sabe nada.
biercEN: A person unacquainted with certain kinds of knowledge familiar to yourself, and having certain other kinds that you know nothing about.
revelationES: Ignorante parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: You talk about Ignoramus as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Secta de herejes españoles de fines del siglo dieciséis; así llamados por ser de peso ligero.
biercEN: A sect of Spanish heretics of the latter part of the sixteenth century; so called because they were light weights-- cunctationes illuminati.
revelationES: Iluminados es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: You name Illuminati and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Convenientemente ubicado para recibir los dardos de la malicia, la envidia y la difamación.
biercEN: Suitably placed for the shafts of malice, envy and detraction.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Ilustre probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: You talk about Illustrious as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Almacén de hechos, de propiedad conjunta del poeta y del mentiroso.
biercEN: A warehouse of facts, with poet and liar in joint ownership.
revelationES: Nadie eligió las reglas de Imaginación. Todos las defienden como si las hubieran escrito ellos.
revelationEN: Imagination demands authenticity, as long as it looks like everyone else’s.

biercES: Especie de inspiración divina, o fuego sagrado, que afecta a los críticos censores de este diccionario.
biercEN: A kind of divine inspiration, or sacred fire affecting censorious critics of this dictionary.
revelationES: Imbecilidad parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: Imbecility is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: Persona poco ilustrada que cree que un país es mejor que otro.
biercEN: An unenlightened person who thinks one country better than another.
revelationES: Le llamas Inmigrante a la costumbre de no cuestionar nada más profundo.
revelationEN: Immigrant is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Que tiene un fuerte sentido del propio mérito, junto con una débil concepción del valor ajeno.
biercEN: Having a strong sense of one's own merit, coupled with a feeble conception of worth in others.
revelationES: Todos usan Inmodesto para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Immodest is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Inconveniente. Todo aquello que, a la larga y en la mayoría de los casos, los hombres consideran generalmente inconveniente termina por considerarse incorrecto, malvado, inmoral.
biercEN: Inexpedient. Whatever in the long run and with regard to the greater number of instances men find to be generally inexpedient comes to be considered wrong, wicked, immoral. If man's notions of right and wrong have any other basis than this of expediency; if they originated, or could have originated, in any other way; if actions have in themselves a moral character apart from, and nowise dependent on, their consequences--then all philosophy is a lie and reason a disorder of the mind.
revelationES: Todos citan Inmoral. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: Immoral is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: En el uso popular, atravesar con cualquier arma que quede fija en la herida. Sin embargo, esto es inexacto: empalar es, propiamente, dar muerte clavando una estaca afilada y vertical a través del cuerpo, dejando a la víctima en posición sentada.
biercEN: In popular usage to pierce with any weapon which remains fixed in the wound. This, however, is inaccurate; to impale is, properly, to put to death by thrusting an upright sharp stake into the body, the victim being left in a sitting position. This was a common mode of punishment among many of the nations of antiquity, and is still in high favor in China and other parts of Asia. Down to the beginning of the fifteenth century it was widely employed in "churching" heretics and schismatics. Wolecraft calls it the "stoole of repentynge," and among the common people it was jocularly known as "riding the one legged horse." Ludwig Salzmann informs us that in Thibet impalement is considered the most appropriate punishment for crimes against religion; and although in China it is sometimes awarded for secular offences, it is most frequently adjudged in cases of sacrilege. To the person in actual experience of impalement it must be a matter of minor importance by what kind of civil or religious dissent he was made acquainted with its discomforts; but doubtless he would feel a certain satisfaction if able to contemplate himself in the character of a weather-cock on the spire of the True Church.
revelationES: Nombras Empalar y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Impale. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: Incapaz de percibir la promesa de una ventaja personal al abrazar cualquiera de los dos bandos de una controversia, o al adoptar cualquiera de dos opiniones contrapuestas.
biercEN: Unable to perceive any promise of personal advantage from espousing either side of a controversy or adopting either of two conflicting opinions.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Imparcial probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: Impartial sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: Estado de ánimo intermedio, en el tiempo, entre el pecado y el castigo.
biercEN: A state of mind intermediate in point of time between sin and punishment.
revelationES: Todos citan Impenitencia. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: Impenitence is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: Tu irreverencia hacia mi divinidad.
biercEN: Your irreverence toward my deity.
revelationES: Impiedad te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: You talk about Impiety as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Acto de bendecir o consagrar mediante la imposición de manos, ceremonia común a muchos sistemas eclesiásticos, pero practicada con la más franca sinceridad por la secta conocida como los Ladrones.
biercEN: The act of blessing or consecrating by the laying on of hands--a ceremony common to many ecclesiastical systems, but performed with the frankest sincerity by the sect known as Thieves.
revelationES: Hablas de Imposición de manos como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: Imposition looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Provisión para las necesidades de hoy con las rentas de mañana.
biercEN: Provision for the needs of to-day from the revenues of to-morrow.
revelationES: Damos por hecho Imprevisión hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: Improvidence is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Riqueza.
biercEN: Wealth.
revelationES: Impunidad es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: Impunity changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: No apto para ser considerado. Se dice de ciertos tipos de testimonio que los jurados se supone incapaces de manejar, y que por eso los jueces descartan incluso en procesos ante ellos mismos. El testimonio de oídas es inadmisible porque quien lo pronunció no juró y no está ante el tribunal para ser examinado; sin embargo, las decisiones más trascendentales, militares, políticas, comerciales y de toda índole, se toman a diario sobre la base de testimonios de oídas. No hay religión en el mundo que se apoye en otra cosa que testimonios de oídas.
biercEN: Not competent to be considered. Said of certain kinds of testimony which juries are supposed to be unfit to be entrusted with, and which judges, therefore, rule out, even of proceedings before themselves alone. Hearsay evidence is inadmissible because the person quoted was unsworn and is not before the court for examination; yet most momentous actions, military, political, commercial and of every other kind, are daily undertaken on hearsay evidence. There is no religion in the world that has any other basis than hearsay evidence. Revelation is hearsay evidence; that the Scriptures are the word of God we have only the testimony of men long dead whose identity is not clearly established and who are not known to have been sworn in any sense. Under the rules of evidence as they now exist in this country, no single assertion in the Bible has in its support any evidence admissible in a court of law. It cannot be proved that the battle of Blenheim ever was fought, that there was such as person as Julius Caesar, such an empire as Assyria.
revelationES: Inadmisible suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Inadmissible to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: De manera poco prometedora, siendo los auspicios desfavorables. Entre los romanos era costumbre, antes de emprender cualquier acción o empresa importante, obtener de los augures algún indicio de su resultado probable; y uno de sus modos favoritos de adivinación consistía en observar el vuelo de las aves, presagios de allí llamados auspicios.
biercEN: In an unpromising manner, the auspices being unfavorable. Among the Romans it was customary before undertaking any important action or enterprise to obtain from the augurs, or state prophets, some hint of its probable outcome; and one of their favorite and most trustworthy modes of divination consisted in observing the flight of birds--the omens thence derived being called auspices. Newspaper reporters and certain miscreant lexicographers have decided that the word--always in the plural--shall mean "patronage" or "management"; as, "The festivities were under the auspices of the Ancient and Honorable Order of Body-Snatchers"; or, "The hilarities were auspicated by the Knights of Hunger."
revelationES: Hablas de Desfavorablemente como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: Inauspiciously changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: La medida natural y racional de la respetabilidad, siendo artificiales, arbitrarios y falaces los criterios habitualmente aceptados; pues, como bien señaló cierto personaje de comedia, 'la verdadera función de la propiedad, cualquiera sea, así como de los honores, títulos y prebendas, no es sino conseguir dinero. De ahí se sigue que todas las cosas deben tasarse según su utilidad para ese fin.'
biercEN: The natural and rational gauge and measure of respectability, the commonly accepted standards being artificial, arbitrary and fallacious; for, as "Sir Sycophas Chrysolater" in the play has justly remarked, "the true use and function of property (in whatsoever it consisteth--coins, or land, or houses, or merchant-stuff, or anything which may be named as holden of right to one's own subservience) as also of honors, titles, preferments and place, and all favor and acquaintance of persons of quality or ableness, are but to get money. Hence it followeth that all things are truly to be rated as of worth in measure of their serviceableness to that end; and their possessors should take rank in agreement thereto, neither the lord of an unproducing manor, howsoever broad and ancient, nor he who bears an unremunerate dignity, nor yet the pauper favorite of a king, being esteemed of level excellency with him whose riches are of daily accretion; and hardly should they whose wealth is barren claim and rightly take more honor than the poor and unworthy."
revelationES: Cuentas Ingreso que no tienes para imaginar la vida que no vas a vivir.
revelationEN: Income is the one god every religion worships without admitting it.

biercES: En el matrimonio, una similitud de gustos, particularmente el gusto por la dominación. La incompatibilidad puede, sin embargo, consistir también en una matrona de mirada mansa que vive a la vuelta de la esquina. Incluso se le ha conocido usar bigote.
biercEN: In matrimony a similarity of tastes, particularly the taste for domination. Incompatibility may, however, consist of a meek-eyed matron living just around the corner. It has even been known to wear a moustache.
revelationES: Incompatibilidad parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: Incompatibility feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: Incapaz de existir si algo más existe. Dos cosas son incompossibles cuando el mundo del ser tiene lugar para una de ellas, pero no para ambas.
biercEN: Unable to exist if something else exists. Two things are incompossible when the world of being has scope enough for one of them, but not enough for both--as Walt Whitman's poetry and God's mercy to man. Incompossibility, it will be seen, is only incompatibility let loose. Instead of such low language as "Go heel yourself--I mean to kill you on sight," the words, "Sir, we are incompossible," would convey an equally significant intimation and in stately courtesy are altogether superior.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Incompatible con la existencia es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: Incompossible looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Miembro de una raza de demonios sumamente inapropiados que, aunque probablemente no del todo extintos, puede decirse que han visto ya sus mejores noches.
biercEN: One of a race of highly improper demons who, though probably not wholly extinct, may be said to have seen their best nights. For a complete account of incubi and succubi, including incubae and succubae, see the Liber Demonorum of Protassus (Paris, 1328), which contains much curious information that would be out of place in a dictionary intended as a text-book for the public schools.
revelationES: Íncubo es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: Nobody tells you, but Incubus is just the elegant way of accepting there is no answer.

biercES: Persona del más vivo interés para los no titulares.
biercEN: A person of the liveliest interest to the outcumbents.
revelationES: Titular te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: Incumbent feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: El elemento principal del éxito; 'pues siendo', dice cierto sabio, 'que hay solo una manera de no hacer nada y diversas maneras de hacer algo, de las cuales, ciertamente, solo una es la correcta, se sigue que quien por indecisión se queda quieto no tiene tantas ocasiones de errar el camino como quien avanza'.
biercEN: The chief element of success; "for whereas," saith Sir Thomas Brewbold, "there is but one way to do nothing and divers way to do something, whereof, to a surety, only one is the right way, it followeth that he who from indecision standeth still hath not so many chances of going astray as he who pusheth forwards"--a most clear and satisfactory exposition of the matter.
revelationES: Hablas de Indecisión como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: Indecision changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Imperfectamente sensible a las distinciones entre las cosas.
biercEN: Imperfectly sensible to distinctions among things.
revelationES: Indiferente es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: You mistake having an opinion about Indifferent for having understood it.

biercES: Enfermedad que el paciente y sus amigos suelen confundir con una profunda convicción religiosa y preocupación por la salvación de la humanidad.
biercEN: A disease which the patient and his friends frequently mistake for deep religious conviction and concern for the salvation of mankind. As the simple Red Man of the western wild put it, with, it must be confessed, a certain force: "Plenty well, no pray; big bellyache, heap God."
revelationES: Damos por hecho Indigestión hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: Indigestion is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: La culpa de la mujer.
biercEN: The guilt of woman.
revelationES: Todos usan Indiscreción para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Indiscretion changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: No calculado para favorecer los propios intereses.
biercEN: Not calculated to advance one's interests.
revelationES: Inconveniente suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Inexpedient sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: El período de nuestra vida en que, según los poetas, 'el Cielo yace a nuestro alrededor'. El mundo empieza a mentirnos poco después.
biercEN: The period of our lives when, according to Wordsworth, "Heaven lies about us." The world begins lying about us pretty soon afterward.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Infancia es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: You name Infancy and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: [Latín] Entre griegos y romanos, sacrificios para propiciar a los Dii Manes, o almas de los héroes muertos; pues los piadosos antiguos no lograban inventar suficientes dioses para satisfacer sus necesidades espirituales, y debían recurrir a varias deidades improvisadas.
biercEN: [Latin] Among the Greeks and Romans, sacrifices for propitiation of the Dii Manes, or souls of the dead heroes; for the pious ancients could not invent enough gods to satisfy their spiritual needs, and had to have a number of makeshift deities, or, as a sailor might say, jury-gods, which they made out of the most unpromising materials. It was while sacrificing a bullock to the spirit of Agamemnon that Laiaides, a priest of Aulis, was favored with an audience of that illustrious warrior's shade, who prophetically recounted to him the birth of Christ and the triumph of Christianity, giving him also a rapid but tolerably complete review of events down to the reign of Saint Louis. The narrative ended abruptly at that point, owing to the inconsiderate crowing of a cock, which compelled the ghosted King of Men to scamper back to Hades. There is a fine mediaeval flavor to this story, and as it has not been traced back further than Pere Brateille, a pious but obscure writer at the court of Saint Louis, we shall probably not err on the side of presumption in considering it apocryphal, though Monsignor Capel's judgment of the matter might be different; and to that I bow--wow.
revelationES: Inferias parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: Inferiae feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: En Nueva York, quien no cree en la religión cristiana; en Constantinopla, quien sí cree. Especie de sinvergüenza imperfectamente reverente, y mezquinamente contribuyente, hacia clérigos, eclesiásticos, papas, pastores, canónigos, monjes, muecines, presbíteros, jerofantes, prelados, curas, misioneros, diáconos, frailes, sumos sacerdotes, brahmanes, confesores, eminencias, ancianos, primados, peregrinos, profetas, imanes, escribas, gurúes, sacristanes, derviches, deanes, cardenales, priores, predicadores, rabinos, ulemas, lamas y demás.
biercEN: In New York, one who does not believe in the Christian religion; in Constantinople, one who does. (See GIAOUR.) A kind of scoundrel imperfectly reverent of, and niggardly contributory to, divines, ecclesiastics, popes, parsons, canons, monks, mollahs, voodoos, presbyters, hierophants, prelates, obeah-men, abbes, nuns, missionaries, exhorters, deacons, friars, hadjis, high-priests, muezzins, brahmins, medicine-men, confessors, eminences, elders, primates, prebendaries, pilgrims, prophets, imaums, beneficiaries, clerks, vicars-choral, archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, preachers, padres, abbotesses, caloyers, palmers, curates, patriarchs, bonezs, santons, beadsmen, canonesses, residentiaries, diocesans, deans, subdeans, rural deans, abdals, charm-sellers, archdeacons, hierarchs, class-leaders, incumbents, capitulars, sheiks, talapoins, postulants, scribes, gooroos, precentors, beadles, fakeers, sextons, reverences, revivalists, cenobites, perpetual curates, chaplains, mudjoes, readers, novices, vicars, pastors, rabbis, ulemas, lamas, sacristans, vergers, dervises, lectors, church wardens, cardinals, prioresses, suffragans, acolytes, rectors, cures, sophis, mutifs and pumpums.
revelationES: Infiel es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: Infidel feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: En política, un quo imaginario que se entrega a cambio de un quid sustancial.
biercEN: In politics, a visionary quo given in exchange for a substantial quid.
revelationES: Buscas el sentido de Influencia toda la vida. Puede que el punto sea justo no encontrarlo.
revelationEN: Influence sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: Aquel que se atreve a creer que Adán no tenía por qué haber pecado, a menos que lo hubiera deseado, en oposición a los Supralapsarios, que sostienen que la caída de aquel desdichado estaba decretada desde el principio.
biercEN: One who ventures to believe that Adam need not have sinned unless he had a mind to--in opposition to the Supralapsarians, who hold that that luckless person's fall was decreed from the beginning. Infralapsarians are sometimes called Sublapsarians without material effect upon the importance and lucidity of their views about Adam.
revelationES: Damos por hecho Infralapsario hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: Infralapsarian changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Aquel que recibe un beneficio de otro, o que de algún modo es objeto de caridad.
biercEN: One who receives a benefit from another, or is otherwise an object of charity.
revelationES: Buscas el sentido de Ingrato toda la vida. Puede que el punto sea justo no encontrarlo.
revelationEN: What you call Ingrate would probably be something else if you had to explain it without help.

biercES: Ofensa un grado por encima, en enormidad, de un desaire.
biercEN: An offense next in degree of enormity to a slight.
revelationES: Todos citan Injuria. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: Injury is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: Carga que, de todas las que cargamos sobre otros y llevamos nosotros mismos, es la más liviana en las manos y la más pesada sobre la espalda.
biercEN: A burden which of all those that we load upon others and carry ourselves is lightest in the hands and heaviest upon the back.
revelationES: Crees que tú usarías Injusticia distinto. Todos lo creyeron antes que tú.
revelationEN: Injustice does not change people. It just reveals what they were already hiding.

biercES: Compuesto villano de tanogalato de hierro, goma arábiga y agua, empleado sobre todo para facilitar el contagio de la idiotez y promover el crimen intelectual. Las propiedades de la tinta son peculiares y contradictorias: sirve para hacer reputaciones y deshacerlas; para ennegrecerlas y para blanquearlas.
biercEN: A villainous compound of tannogallate of iron, gum-arabic and water, chiefly used to facilitate the infection of idiocy and promote intellectual crime. The properties of ink are peculiar and contradictory: it may be used to make reputations and unmake them; to blacken them and to make them white; but it is most generally and acceptably employed as a mortar to bind together the stones of an edifice of fame, and as a whitewash to conceal afterward the rascal quality of the material. There are men called journalists who have established ink baths which some persons pay money to get into, others to get out of. Not infrequently it occurs that a person who has paid to get in pays twice as much to get out.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Tinta probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Ink. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: Natural, inherente; como las ideas innatas, es decir, ideas con las que nacemos, por habérsenos impartido previamente. La doctrina de las ideas innatas es una de las fes más admirables de la filosofía, siendo ella misma una idea innata y, por tanto, inaccesible a toda refutación.
biercEN: Natural, inherent--as innate ideas, that is to say, ideas that we are born with, having had them previously imparted to us. The doctrine of innate ideas is one of the most admirable faiths of philosophy, being itself an innate idea and therefore inaccessible to disproof, though Locke foolishly supposed himself to have given it "a black eye." Among innate ideas may be mentioned the belief in one's ability to conduct a newspaper, in the greatness of one's country, in the superiority of one's civilization, in the importance of one's personal affairs and in the interesting nature of one's diseases.
revelationES: Innato te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: Nobody tells you, but Innate is just the elegant way of accepting there is no answer.

biercES: El estómago, el corazón, el alma y demás vísceras. Muchos eminentes investigadores no clasifican al alma entre las entrañas, pero cierto observador agudo está persuadido de que el misterioso órgano llamado bazo no es sino nuestra parte inmortal.
biercEN: The stomach, heart, soul and other bowels. Many eminent investigators do not class the soul as an in'ard, but that acute observer and renowned authority, Dr. Gunsaulus, is persuaded that the mysterious organ known as the spleen is nothing less than our immortal part. To the contrary, Professor Garrett P. Servis holds that man's soul is that prolongation of his spinal marrow which forms the pith of his no tail; and for demonstration of his faith points confidently to the fact that tailed animals have no souls. Concerning these two theories, it is best to suspend judgment by believing both.
revelationES: Entrañas suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: You assumed In'Ards for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Algo escrito sobre otra cosa. Las inscripciones son de muchas clases, pero sobre todo conmemorativas, destinadas a perpetuar la fama de alguna persona ilustre y transmitir a épocas lejanas el registro de sus servicios y virtudes.
biercEN: Something written on another thing. Inscriptions are of many kinds, but mostly memorial, intended to commemorate the fame of some illustrious person and hand down to distant ages the record of his services and virtues. To this class of inscriptions belongs the name of John Smith, penciled on the Washington monument. Following are examples of memorial inscriptions on tombstones: (See EPITAPH.)
revelationES: Inscripción suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Inscription is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Ingenioso juego de azar moderno en el que se permite al jugador disfrutar de la reconfortante convicción de que le está ganando a la banca.
biercEN: An ingenious modern game of chance in which the player is permitted to enjoy the comfortable conviction that he is beating the man who keeps the table.
revelationES: Seguro suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: You assumed Insurance for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Revolución fracasada. El fracaso del descontento en sustituir la anarquía por el mal gobierno.
biercEN: An unsuccessful revolution. Disaffection's failure to substitute misrule for bad government.
revelationES: Todos citan Insurrección. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: You talk about Insurrection as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: El sentido que tiene la mente de la preponderancia de un conjunto de influencias sobre otro; efecto cuya causa es la inminencia, próxima o remota, de la realización de un acto involuntario.
biercEN: The mind's sense of the prevalence of one set of influences over another set; an effect whose cause is the imminence, immediate or remote, of the performance of an involuntary act.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Intención es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: You search for the meaning of Intention your whole life. Maybe the point is exactly not finding it.

biercES: Aquel que permite a dos personas de idiomas distintos entenderse, repitiendo a cada una lo que le habría convenido al intérprete que la otra hubiera dicho.
biercEN: One who enables two persons of different languages to understand each other by repeating to each what it would have been to the interpreter's advantage for the other to have said.
revelationES: Nombras Intérprete y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Interpreter. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: Período durante el cual un país monárquico es gobernado por una mancha tibia sobre el almohadón del trono.
biercEN: The period during which a monarchical country is governed by a warm spot on the cushion of the throne. The experiment of letting the spot grow cold has commonly been attended by most unhappy results from the zeal of many worthy persons to make it warm again.
revelationES: Hablas de Interregno como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: You assumed Interregnum for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Relación hacia la cual los necios son providencialmente atraídos para su mutua destrucción.
biercEN: A relation into which fools are providentially drawn for their mutual destruction.
revelationES: Hablas de Intimidad como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: Intimacy is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Ceremonia social inventada por el diablo para la gratificación de sus siervos y el tormento de sus enemigos.
biercEN: A social ceremony invented by the devil for the gratification of his servants and the plaguing of his enemies. The introduction attains its most malevolent development in this country, being, indeed, closely related to our political system. Every American being the equal of every other American, it follows that everybody has the right to know everybody else, which implies the right to introduce without request or permission. The Declaration of Independence should have read thus:
revelationES: Damos por hecho Presentación hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: You call Introduction the habit of never questioning anything deeper.

biercES: Persona que construye un ingenioso ordenamiento de ruedas, palancas y resortes, y cree que eso es civilización.
biercEN: A person who makes an ingenious arrangement of wheels, levers and springs, and believes it civilization.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Inventor es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: Nobody tells you, but Inventor is just the elegant way of accepting there is no answer.

biercES: La principal de las grandes fes del mundo.
biercEN: The principal one of the great faiths of the world.
revelationES: Diste por sentado Irreligión durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: You call Irreligion the habit of never questioning anything deeper.

biercES: El patriotismo de un escocés.
biercEN: The patriotism of a Scotchman.
revelationES: Sarna es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: You search for the meaning of Itch your whole life. Maybe the point is exactly not finding it.

biercES: Indebidamente preocupado por preservar aquello que solo puede perderse si no vale la pena conservarlo.
biercEN: Unduly concerned about the preservation of that which can be lost only if not worth keeping.
revelationES: Celoso cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Jealous is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: Antiguo funcionario adscrito a la casa de un rey, cuyo oficio era divertir a la corte con acciones y dichos ridículos, atestiguados como tales por su traje abigarrado. El propio rey vestía con dignidad, y el mundo tardó siglos en descubrir que su propia conducta y sus decretos eran suficientemente ridículos como para divertir no solo a su corte, sino a toda la humanidad.
biercEN: An officer formerly attached to a king's household, whose business it was to amuse the court by ludicrous actions and utterances, the absurdity being attested by his motley costume. The king himself being attired with dignity, it took the world some centuries to discover that his own conduct and decrees were sufficiently ridiculous for the amusement not only of his court but of all mankind. The jester was commonly called a fool, but the poets and romancers have ever delighted to represent him as a singularly wise and witty person. In the circus of to-day the melancholy ghost of the court fool effects the dejection of humbler audiences with the same jests wherewith in life he gloomed the marble hall, panged the patrician sense of humor and tapped the tank of royal tears.
revelationES: Todos usan Bufón para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Jester looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Instrumento poco musical, que se toca sosteniéndolo firme con los dientes e intentando espantarlo con el dedo.
biercEN: An unmusical instrument, played by holding it fast with the teeth and trying to brush it away with the finger.
revelationES: Hablas de Birimbao como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: You talk about Jews-Harp as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Pequeñas varitas que los chinos queman en sus payasadas paganas, a imitación de ciertos ritos sagrados de nuestra santa religión.
biercEN: Small sticks burned by the Chinese in their pagan tomfoolery, in imitation of certain sacred rites of our holy religion.
revelationES: Damos por hecho Varitas de incienso hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: You take Joss-Sticks for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: Mercancía, en condición más o menos adulterada, que el Estado le vende al ciudadano como recompensa por su lealtad, sus impuestos y sus servicios personales.
biercEN: A commodity which is a more or less adulterated condition the State sells to the citizen as a reward for his allegiance, taxes and personal service.
revelationES: Justicia corrompe. Lo interesante es lo rápido que encuentras la excusa.
revelationEN: You seek Justice to feel safe. You just change what you are afraid of.

biercES: Crear una vacante sin nominar sucesor.
biercEN: To create a vacancy without nominating a successor.
revelationES: Matar parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: You assumed Kill for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Vestimenta que a veces usan los escoceses en América, y los americanos en Escocia.
biercEN: A costume sometimes worn by Scotchmen in America and Americans in Scotland.
revelationES: Le llamas Kilt a la costumbre de no cuestionar nada más profundo.
revelationEN: You call Kilt the habit of never questioning anything deeper.

biercES: Breve prefacio a diez volúmenes de exigencias.
biercEN: A brief preface to ten volumes of exaction.
revelationES: Le llamas Amabilidad a la costumbre de no cuestionar nada más profundo.
revelationEN: Kindness is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Varón comúnmente conocido en América como 'cabeza coronada', aunque nunca usa corona y por lo general carece de cabeza digna de mención.
biercEN: A male person commonly known in America as a "crowned head," although he never wears a crown and has usually no head to speak of.
revelationES: Rey no cambia a las personas. Solo revela lo que ya escondían.
revelationEN: The history of King is written by whoever had it, not whoever suffered it.

biercES: Dolencia que antiguamente se curaba con el toque del soberano, pero que ahora deben tratar los médicos.
biercEN: A malady that was formerly cured by the touch of the sovereign, but has now to be treated by the physicians. Thus "the most pious Edward" of England used to lay his royal hand upon the ailing subjects and make them whole--
revelationES: Nadie renuncia a Mal del rey por convicción. Renuncian cuando ya no pueden sostenerlo.
revelationEN: Everyone says they hate King'S Evil. Everyone would take a little, in private.

biercES: Palabra inventada por los poetas como rima. Se supone que significa, en términos generales, algún tipo de rito o ceremonia relacionado con un buen entendimiento, aunque este lexicógrafo desconoce el modo en que se ejecuta.
biercEN: A word invented by the poets as a rhyme for "bliss." It is supposed to signify, in a general way, some kind of rite or ceremony appertaining to a good understanding; but the manner of its performance is unknown to this lexicographer.
revelationES: Beso perdona todo la primera vez. Cuenta cada vez después.
revelationEN: Kiss makes you promise things sanity would never sign off on.

biercES: Un ladrón rico.
biercEN: A rich thief.
revelationES: Crees entender Cleptómano. La verdad es que nadie lo sabe, y actúan con tu misma confianza.
revelationEN: Kleptomaniac is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Libro que los mahometanos creen neciamente escrito por inspiración divina, pero que los cristianos saben que es una impostura perversa, contradictoria con las Sagradas Escrituras.
biercEN: A book which the Mohammedans foolishly believe to have been written by divine inspiration, but which Christians know to be a wicked imposture, contradictory to the Holy Scriptures.
revelationES: Corán te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: Koran feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: Uno de los procesos por los cuales A adquiere propiedad para B.
biercEN: One of the processes by which A acquires property for B.
revelationES: Todos hablan de Trabajo en el currículum. Nadie lo pone en la lápida.
revelationEN: Labor is a race against people who never knew they were competing with you.

biercES: Parte de la superficie terrestre, considerada como propiedad. La teoría de que la tierra es propiedad sujeta a dominio privado es el fundamento de la sociedad moderna, y es eminentemente digna de la superestructura que sostiene. Llevada a su conclusión lógica, significa que algunos tienen el derecho de impedir que otros vivan.
biercEN: A part of the earth's surface, considered as property. The theory that land is property subject to private ownership and control is the foundation of modern society, and is eminently worthy of the superstructure. Carried to its logical conclusion, it means that some have the right to prevent others from living; for the right to own implies the right exclusively to occupy; and in fact laws of trespass are enacted wherever property in land is recognized. It follows that if the whole area of terra firma is owned by A, B and C, there will be no place for D, E, F and G to be born, or, born as trespassers, to exist.
revelationES: Hablas de Tierra como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: You take Land for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: La música con la que encantamos a las serpientes que custodian el tesoro ajeno.
biercEN: The music with which we charm the serpents guarding another's treasure.
revelationES: Lenguaje cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: You search for the meaning of Language your whole life. Maybe the point is exactly not finding it.

biercES: Célebre pieza escultórica de la Antigüedad que representa a un sacerdote de ese nombre y a sus dos hijos entre los anillos de dos enormes serpientes. La habilidad y diligencia con que el anciano y los muchachos sostienen a las serpientes y las mantienen ocupadas en su tarea han sido justamente consideradas una de las más nobles ilustraciones artísticas del dominio de la inteligencia humana sobre la inercia bruta.
biercEN: A famous piece of antique scripture representing a priest of that name and his two sons in the folds of two enormous serpents. The skill and diligence with which the old man and lads support the serpents and keep them up to their work have been justly regarded as one of the noblest artistic illustrations of the mastery of human intelligence over brute inertia.
revelationES: Laoconte suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Laocoon changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Uno de los órganos más importantes del sistema femenino: admirable previsión de la naturaleza para el reposo de la infancia, aunque principalmente útil, en las festividades rurales, para sostener platos de pollo frío y cabezas de varones adultos.
biercEN: One of the most important organs of the female system--an admirable provision of nature for the repose of infancy, but chiefly useful in rural festivities to support plates of cold chicken and heads of adult males. The male of our species has a rudimentary lap, imperfectly developed and in no way contributing to the animal's substantial welfare.
revelationES: Diste por sentado Regazo durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: Lap is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Instrumento del zapatero, nombrado por una Providencia ceñuda como oportunidad para el hacedor de juegos de palabras.
biercEN: A shoemaker's implement, named by a frowning Providence as opportunity to the maker of puns.
revelationES: Damos por hecho Horma hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: You call Last the habit of never questioning anything deeper.

biercES: Convulsión interior que produce una distorsión de las facciones, acompañada de ruidos inarticulados. Es contagiosa y, aunque intermitente, incurable. La propensión a los ataques de risa es una de las características que distinguen al hombre de los animales.
biercEN: An interior convulsion, producing a distortion of the features and accompanied by inarticulate noises. It is infectious and, though intermittent, incurable. Liability to attacks of laughter is one of the characteristics distinguishing man from the animals-- these being not only inaccessible to the provocation of his example, but impregnable to the microbes having original jurisdiction in bestowal of the disease. Whether laughter could be imparted to animals by inoculation from the human patient is a question that has not been answered by experimentation. Dr. Meir Witchell holds that the infectious character of laughter is due to the instantaneous fermentation of sputa diffused in a spray. From this peculiarity he names the disorder Convulsio spargens.
revelationES: Risa suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: You mistake having an opinion about Laughter for having understood it.

biercES: Coronado con hojas de laurel. En Inglaterra, el Poeta Laureado es un oficial de la corte del soberano, que actúa como esqueleto danzante en cada festín real y como plañidero mudo en cada funeral real.
biercEN: Crowned with leaves of the laurel. In England the Poet Laureate is an officer of the sovereign's court, acting as dancing skeleton at every royal feast and singing-mute at every royal funeral. Of all incumbents of that high office, Robert Southey had the most notable knack at drugging the Samson of public joy and cutting his hair to the quick; and he had an artistic color-sense which enabled him so to blacken a public grief as to give it the aspect of a national crime.
revelationES: Laureado parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: Laureate feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: El laurus, vegetal dedicado a Apolo, y antiguamente deshojado para coronar las sienes de los vencedores y de los poetas con influencia en la corte.
biercEN: The laurus, a vegetable dedicated to Apollo, and formerly defoliated to wreathe the brows of victors and such poets as had influence at court. (Vide supra.)
revelationES: Laurel cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Laurel changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Compatible con la voluntad de un juez con jurisdicción.
biercEN: Compatible with the will of a judge having jurisdiction.
revelationES: Buscas Legal para sentirte seguro. Solo cambias de qué tienes miedo.
revelationEN: Everyone says they hate Lawful. Everyone would take a little, in private.

biercES: Aquel versado en la elusión de la ley.
biercEN: One skilled in circumvention of the law.
revelationES: Buscas Abogado para sentirte seguro. Solo cambias de qué tienes miedo.
revelationEN: Lawyer works best when nobody notices you are using it.

biercES: Reposo injustificado de modales en una persona de baja condición.
biercEN: Unwarranted repose of manner in a person of low degree.
revelationES: Confundes Pereza con estar ocupado. El reloj no distingue.
revelationEN: You chase Laziness your whole life. The moment you get it, you already want something else.

biercES: Metal pesado, gris azulado, muy usado para dar estabilidad a los amantes ligeros, en particular a quienes aman no sabiamente, sino a la esposa de otro. El plomo también presta gran servicio como contrapeso para un argumento tan pesado que inclina la balanza del debate en la dirección equivocada.
biercEN: A heavy blue-gray metal much used in giving stability to light lovers--particularly to those who love not wisely but other men's wives. Lead is also of great service as a counterpoise to an argument of such weight that it turns the scale of debate the wrong way. An interesting fact in the chemistry of international controversy is that at the point of contact of two patriotisms lead is precipitated in great quantities.
revelationES: Plomo suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Lead is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: La clase de ignorancia que distingue a los estudiosos.
biercEN: The kind of ignorance distinguishing the studious.
revelationES: Saber cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Learning to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: Alguien con la mano en tu bolsillo, la lengua en tu oído y su fe puesta en tu paciencia.
biercEN: One with his hand in your pocket, his tongue in your ear and his faith in your patience.
revelationES: Crees entender Conferencista. La verdad es que nadie lo sabe, y actúan con tu misma confianza.

biercES: Hierba del género Lactuca, 'con la cual', dice cierto piadoso gastrónomo, 'a Dios le ha placido premiar al bueno y castigar al malvado'.
biercEN: An herb of the genus Lactuca, "Wherewith," says that pious gastronome, Hengist Pelly, "God has been pleased to reward the good and punish the wicked. For by his inner light the righteous man has discerned a manner of compounding for it a dressing to the appetency whereof a multitude of gustible condiments conspire, being reconciled and ameliorated with profusion of oil, the entire comestible making glad the heart of the godly and causing his face to shine. But the person of spiritual unworth is successfully tempted to the Adversary to eat of lettuce with destitution of oil, mustard, egg, salt and garlic, and with a rascal bath of vinegar polluted with sugar. Wherefore the person of spiritual unworth suffers an intestinal pang of strange complexity and raises the song."
revelationES: Lechuga suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Lettuce to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: Enorme animal acuático mencionado en el libro de Job. Algunos suponen que era la ballena, pero cierto distinguido ictiólogo sostiene con considerable vehemencia que se trataba de una especie de renacuajo gigantesco.
biercEN: An enormous aquatic animal mentioned by Job. Some suppose it to have been the whale, but that distinguished ichthyologer, Dr. Jordan, of Stanford University, maintains with considerable heat that it was a species of gigantic Tadpole (Thaddeus Polandensis) or Polliwig--Maria pseudo-hirsuta. For an exhaustive description and history of the Tadpole consult the famous monograph of Jane Potter, Thaddeus of Warsaw.
revelationES: Nombras Leviatán y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: You assumed Leviathan for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Sujeto pestilente que, con el pretexto de registrar cierta etapa del desarrollo de una lengua, hace cuanto puede por detener su crecimiento, endurecer su flexibilidad y mecanizar sus procedimientos. Pues el lexicógrafo, una vez escrito su diccionario, pasa a ser considerado 'como quien tiene autoridad', cuando su función es únicamente dejar constancia, no dictar ley.
biercEN: A pestilent fellow who, under the pretense of recording some particular stage in the development of a language, does what he can to arrest its growth, stiffen its flexibility and mechanize its methods. For your lexicographer, having written his dictionary, comes to be considered "as one having authority," whereas his function is only to make a record, not to give a law. The natural servility of the human understanding having invested him with judicial power, surrenders its right of reason and submits itself to a chronicle as if it were a statute. Let the dictionary (for example) mark a good word as "obsolete" or "obsolescent" and few men thereafter venture to use it, whatever their need of it and however desirable its restoration to favor--whereby the process of impoverishment is accelerated and speech decays. On the contrary, the bold and discerning writer who, recognizing the truth that language must grow by innovation if it grow at all, makes new words and uses the old in an unfamiliar sense, has no following and is tartly reminded that "it isn't in the dictionary" --although down to the time of the first lexicographer (Heaven forgive him!) no author ever had used a word that was in the dictionary. In the golden prime and high noon of English speech; when from the lips of the great Elizabethans fell words that made their own meaning and carried it in their very sound; when a Shakespeare and a Bacon were possible, and the language now rapidly perishing at one end and slowly renewed at the other was in vigorous growth and hardy preservation--sweeter than honey and stronger than a lion--the lexicographer was a person unknown, the dictionary a creation which his Creator had not created him to create.
revelationES: Lexicógrafo parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: Lexicographer changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Funcionario útil, no infrecuentemente hallado en la dirección de un periódico. En su carácter de editor está estrechamente emparentado con el chantajista por lazo de ocasional identidad; pues en verdad el adulón servil no es sino el chantajista bajo otro aspecto.
biercEN: A useful functionary, not infrequently found editing a newspaper. In his character of editor he is closely allied to the blackmailer by the tie of occasional identity; for in truth the lickspittle is only the blackmailer under another aspect, although the latter is frequently found as an independent species. Lickspittling is more detestable than blackmailing, precisely as the business of a confidence man is more detestable than that of a highway robber; and the parallel maintains itself throughout, for whereas few robbers will cheat, every sneak will plunder if he dare.
revelationES: Crees entender Adulón servil. La verdad es que nadie lo sabe, y actúan con tu misma confianza.

La pregunta '¿vale la pena vivir?' ha sido muy discutida, particularmente por aquellos que creen que no, muchos de los cuales han escrito extensamente en apoyo de su tesis y, gracias a la cuidadosa observancia de las leyes de la salud, disfrutado durante largos años los honores de una controversia exitosa.
biercEN: A spiritual pickle preserving the body from decay. We live in daily apprehension of its loss; yet when lost it is not missed. The question, "Is life worth living?" has been much discussed; particularly by those who think it is not, many of whom have written at great length in support of their view and by careful observance of the laws of health enjoyed for long terms of years the honors of successful controversy.
revelationES: Crees entender Vida. La verdad es que nadie lo sabe, y actúan con tu misma confianza.
revelationEN: Life is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

The sentiments and emotions which every literary anatomist now knows to haunt the heart were anciently believed to infest the liver; and even Gascoygne, speaking of the emotional side of human nature, calls it "our hepaticall parte." It was at one time considered the seat of life; hence its name--liver, the thing we live with. The liver is heaven's best gift to the goose; without it that bird would be unable to supply us with the Strasbourg pate.

biercES: Conocimiento, particularmente el que no proviene de un curso regular de instrucción, sino de la lectura de libros ocultos, o de la naturaleza misma. Este último se designa comúnmente como folclore, y abarca mitos y supersticiones populares.
biercEN: Learning--particularly that sort which is not derived from a regular course of instruction but comes of the reading of occult books, or by nature. This latter is commonly designated as folk-lore and embraces popularly myths and superstitions. In Baring-Gould's Curious Myths of the Middle Ages the reader will find many of these traced backward, through various peoples on converging lines, toward a common origin in remote antiquity. Among these are the fables of "Teddy the Giant Killer," "The Sleeping John Sharp Williams," "Little Red Riding Hood and the Sugar Trust," "Beauty and the Brisbane," "The Seven Aldermen of Ephesus," "Rip Van Fairbanks," and so forth. The fable which Goethe so affectingly relates under the title of "The Erl-King" was known two thousand years ago in Greece as "The Demos and the Infant Industry." One of the most general and ancient of these myths is that Arabian tale of "Ali Baba and the Forty Rockefellers."
revelationES: Saber tradicional cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: What you call Lore would probably be something else if you had to explain it without help.

biercES: Privación de aquello que teníamos, o que no teníamos. Así, en este segundo sentido, se dice de un candidato derrotado que 'perdió su elección'.
biercEN: Privation of that which we had, or had not. Thus, in the latter sense, it is said of a defeated candidate that he "lost his election"; and of that eminent man, the poet Gilder, that he has "lost his mind." It is in the former and more legitimate sense, that the word is used in the famous epitaph:
revelationES: Pérdida es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.

biercES: Locura temporal, curable mediante el matrimonio o el alejamiento del paciente de las influencias bajo las cuales contrajo el trastorno. Esta enfermedad, como la caries y otras dolencias, prevalece solo entre las razas civilizadas que viven en condiciones artificiales; las naciones bárbaras, que respiran aire puro y comen alimentos simples, gozan de inmunidad ante sus estragos.
biercEN: A temporary insanity curable by marriage or by removal of the patient from the influences under which he incurred the disorder. This disease, like caries and many other ailments, is prevalent only among civilized races living under artificial conditions; barbarous nations breathing pure air and eating simple food enjoy immunity from its ravages. It is sometimes fatal, but more frequently to the physician than to the patient.
revelationES: Juraste que Amor sería para siempre. "Para siempre" duró lo que dura la novedad.

biercES: Aquel olvidado por los dioses, que vive hasta una edad avanzada. La historia abunda en ejemplos, desde Matusalén hasta ancianos legendarios más recientes.
biercEN: One forgotten of the gods and living to a great age. History is abundantly supplied with examples, from Methuselah to Old Parr, but some notable instances of longevity are less well known. A Calabrian peasant named Coloni, born in 1753, lived so long that he had what he considered a glimpse of the dawn of universal peace. Scanavius relates that he knew an archbishop who was so old that he could remember a time when he did not deserve hanging. In 1566 a linen draper of Bristol, England, declared that he had lived five hundred years, and that in all that time he had never told a lie. There are instances of longevity (macrobiosis) in our own country. Senator Chauncey Depew is old enough to know better. The editor of The American, a newspaper in New York City, has a memory that goes back to the time when he was a rascal, but not to the fact. The President of the United States was born so long ago that many of the friends of his youth have risen to high political and military preferment without the assistance of personal merit. The verses following were written by a macrobian:
revelationES: Macrobio es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.

biercES: Afectado por un alto grado de independencia intelectual; que no se ajusta a los estándares de pensamiento, habla y acción derivados por los conformistas del estudio de sí mismos; en desacuerdo con la mayoría; en suma, poco común.
biercEN: Affected with a high degree of intellectual independence; not conforming to standards of thought, speech and action derived by the conformants from study of themselves; at odds with the majority; in short, unusual. It is noteworthy that persons are pronounced mad by officials destitute of evidence that themselves are sane. For illustration, this present (and illustrious) lexicographer is no firmer in the faith of his own sanity than is any inmate of any madhouse in the land; yet for aught he knows to the contrary, instead of the lofty occupation that seems to him to be engaging his powers he may really be beating his hands against the window bars of an asylum and declaring himself Noah Webster, to the innocent delight of many thoughtless spectators.
revelationES: Loco te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.

biercES: Habitante de Magdala. Popularmente, una mujer descubierta en falta. Esta definición cuenta con la autoridad de la ignorancia, siendo María de Magdala una persona distinta de la mujer arrepentida que menciona San Lucas.
biercEN: An inhabitant of Magdala. Popularly, a woman found out. This definition of the word has the authority of ignorance, Mary of Magdala being another person than the penitent woman mentioned by St. Luke. It has also the official sanction of the governments of Great Britain and the United States. In England the word is pronounced Maudlin, whence maudlin, adjective, unpleasantly sentimental. With their Maudlin for Magdalene, and their Bedlam for Bethlehem, the English may justly boast themselves the greatest of revisers.
revelationES: Buscas el sentido de Magdalena toda la vida. Puede que el punto sea justo no encontrarlo.

biercEN: Having a grandeur or splendor superior to that to which the spectator is accustomed, as the ears of an ass, to a rabbit, or the glory of a glowworm, to a maggot.

revelationEN: Magnificent changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Tamaño. Siendo la magnitud puramente relativa, nada es grande y nada es pequeño. Si todo en el universo se incrementara en volumen mil diámetros, nada sería más grande que antes.
biercEN: Size. Magnitude being purely relative, nothing is large and nothing small. If everything in the universe were increased in bulk one thousand diameters nothing would be any larger than it was before, but if one thing remain unchanged all the others would be larger than they had been. To an understanding familiar with the relativity of magnitude and distance the spaces and masses of the astronomer would be no more impressive than those of the microscopist. For anything we know to the contrary, the visible universe may be a small part of an atom, with its component ions, floating in the life-fluid (luminiferous ether) of some animal. Possibly the wee creatures peopling the corpuscles of our own blood are overcome with the proper emotion when contemplating the unthinkable distance from one of these to another.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Magnitud es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: You think you understand Magnitude. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Ave cuya disposición al hurto sugirió a alguien que podría enseñársele a hablar.

The genus has a wide geographical distribution, being found wherever sought and deplored wherever found. The maiden is not altogether unpleasing to the eye, nor (without her piano and her views) insupportable to the ear, though in respect to comeliness distinctly inferior to the rainbow, and, with regard to the part of her that is audible, bleaten out of the field by the canary--which, also, is more portable.

revelationES: Majestad es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: You talk about Majesty as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Miembro del sexo desestimado, o prescindible. El varón de la especie humana es comúnmente conocido (por la mujer) como Mero Hombre. El género tiene dos variedades: los buenos proveedores y los malos proveedores.
biercEN: A member of the unconsidered, or negligible sex. The male of the human race is commonly known (to the female) as Mere Man. The genus has two varieties: good providers and bad providers.
revelationES: Todos citan Varón. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: Male changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: El factor principal del progreso de la raza humana.
biercEN: The chief factor in the progress of the human race.
revelationES: Malhechor parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: You think you understand Malefactor. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Relativo a Malthus y sus doctrinas. Malthus creía en limitar artificialmente la población, pero descubrió que no podía lograrse solo con palabras.
biercEN: Pertaining to Malthus and his doctrines. Malthus believed in artificially limiting population, but found that it could not be done by talking. One of the most practical exponents of the Malthusian idea was Herod of Judea, though all the famous soldiers have been of the same way of thinking.
revelationES: Malthusiano es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: Malthusian is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Familia de animales vertebrados cuyas hembras, en estado natural, amamantan a sus crías, pero que, civilizadas e ilustradas, las envían a una nodriza, o usan mamadera.
biercEN: A family of vertebrate animals whose females in a state of nature suckle their young, but when civilized and enlightened put them out to nurse, or use the bottle.
revelationES: Damos por hecho Mamíferos hasta que un día falta, y ahí recién le prestamos atención.
revelationEN: Mammalia is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: El dios de la religión más importante del mundo. Su templo principal está en la ciudad santa de Nueva York.
biercEN: The god of the world's leading religion. The chief temple is in the holy city of New York.
revelationES: Mammón es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: You take Mammon for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: Animal tan perdido en la arrobada contemplación de lo que cree ser, que pasa por alto lo que indudablemente debería ser. Su principal ocupación es exterminar a otros animales y a su propia especie, la cual, sin embargo, se multiplica con tan insistente rapidez que infesta la tierra habitable entera.
biercEN: An animal so lost in rapturous contemplation of what he thinks he is as to overlook what he indubitably ought to be. His chief occupation is extermination of other animals and his own species, which, however, multiplies with such insistent rapidity as to infest the whole habitable earth and Canada.
revelationES: Hombre es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: You call Man the habit of never questioning anything deeper.

biercES: Las partes inmortales de griegos y romanos muertos. Se hallaban en un estado de sordo malestar hasta que los cuerpos de los que habían exhalado eran enterrados y quemados; y no parecen haber sido particularmente felices después.
biercEN: The immortal parts of dead Greeks and Romans. They were in a state of dull discomfort until the bodies from which they had exhaled were buried and burned; and they seem not to have been particularly happy afterward.
revelationES: Nombras Manes y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: You name Manes and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Antigua doctrina persa de una guerra incesante entre el Bien y el Mal. Cuando el Bien abandonó la lucha, los persas se unieron a la Oposición victoriosa.
biercEN: The ancient Persian doctrine of an incessant warfare between Good and Evil. When Good gave up the fight the Persians joined the victorious Opposition.
revelationES: Todos citan Maniqueísmo. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: You call Manicheism the habit of never questioning anything deeper.

biercES: Alimento dado milagrosamente a los israelitas en el desierto. Cuando dejó de suministrárseles, se asentaron y labraron la tierra, fertilizándola, por lo general, con los cuerpos de los ocupantes originales.
biercEN: A food miraculously given to the Israelites in the wilderness. When it was no longer supplied to them they settled down and tilled the soil, fertilizing it, as a rule, with the bodies of the original occupants.
revelationES: Maná es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: Manna looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: El estado o condición de una comunidad compuesta por un amo, una ama y dos esclavos, lo que hace, en total, dos.
biercEN: The state or condition of a community consisting of a master, a mistress and two slaves, making in all, two.
revelationES: Nadie te enseñó que Matrimonio también se factura en silencios, no solo en besos.
revelationEN: You search for real Marriage. You settle for whatever shows up once you are tired of searching.

biercES: Aquel que avanza por la línea de menor resistencia hacia una muerte deseada.
biercEN: One who moves along the line of least reluctance to a desired death.
revelationES: Mártir es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: Martyr is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Que tiene existencia real, a diferencia de una imaginaria. Importante.
biercEN: Having an actual existence, as distinguished from an imaginary one. Important.
revelationES: Material es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: Material is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: La última y más graciosa necedad de los ricos.
biercEN: The final and funniest folly of the rich.
revelationES: Mausoleo cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: You assumed Mausoleum for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Una de las salsas que sirven a los franceses en lugar de religión de Estado.
biercEN: One of the sauces which serve the French in place of a state religion.
revelationES: Mayonesa es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: You name Mayonnaise and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: El caso objetable de Yo. El pronombre personal tiene tres casos: el dominante, el objetable y el opresivo. Cada uno es los tres a la vez.
biercEN: The objectionable case of I. The personal pronoun in English has three cases, the dominative, the objectionable and the oppressive. Each is all three.
revelationES: Mí es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: You think you understand Me. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Avanzar sinuosa y sin rumbo. La palabra es el antiguo nombre de un río que torcía y se retorcía en el esfuerzo por alejarse del alcance del oído cuando griegos y troyanos se jactaban de sus proezas.
biercEN: To proceed sinuously and aimlessly. The word is the ancient name of a river about one hundred and fifty miles south of Troy, which turned and twisted in the effort to get out of hearing when the Greeks and Trojans boasted of their prowess.
revelationES: Serpentear es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: You search for the meaning of Meander your whole life. Maybe the point is exactly not finding it.

biercES: Pequeño disco de metal que se entrega como recompensa por virtudes, logros o servicios más o menos auténticos.
biercEN: A small metal disk given as a reward for virtues, attainments or services more or less authentic.
revelationES: Nombras Medalla y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: You take Medal for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: Una piedra arrojada en un barrio para matar a un perro en otro.
biercEN: A stone flung down the Bowery to kill a dog in Broadway.
revelationES: Todos citan Medicina. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: You call Medicine the habit of never questioning anything deeper.
