biercEN: Dedicated to some religious purpose; having a divine character; inspiring solemn thoughts or emotions; as, the Dalai Lama of Thibet; the Moogum of M'bwango; the temple of Apes in Ceylon; the Cow in India; the Crocodile, the Cat and the Onion of ancient Egypt; the Mufti of Moosh; the hair of the dog that bit Noah, etc.
revelationES: Sagrado es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: Sacred is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Mamífero vertebrado que sostiene las opiniones políticas de cierto demagogo notorio, cuyas audiencias se reunían en los espacios abiertos (arenales) de la ciudad. Fiel a las tradiciones de su especie, este líder del proletariado terminó siendo comprado por sus enemigos del orden y la ley, viviendo próspero en silencio y muriendo impenitentemente rico.
biercEN: A vertebrate mammal holding the political views of Denis Kearney, a notorious demagogue of San Francisco, whose audiences gathered in the open spaces (sandlots) of the town. True to the traditions of his species, this leader of the proletariat was finally bought off by his law-and-order enemies, living prosperously silent and dying impenitently rich. But before his treason he imposed upon California a constitution that was a confection of sin in a diction of solecisms. The similarity between the words "sandlotter" and "sansculotte" is problematically significant, but indubitably suggestive.
revelationES: Agitador de arenal es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: Sandlotter is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Dispositivo mecánico que actúa automáticamente para impedir la caída de un ascensor, o jaula, en caso de accidente del aparato de izaje.
biercEN: A mechanical device acting automatically to prevent the fall of an elevator, or cage, in case of an accident to the hoisting apparatus.
revelationES: Freno de seguridad es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: You name Safety-Clutch and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Un pecador muerto, revisado y editado.
biercEN: A dead sinner revised and edited.
revelationES: Santo te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: Saint looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Cierta cualidad literaria frecuentemente observada en las novelas populares, especialmente en las escritas por mujeres y jovencitas, que le dan otro nombre y creen que al introducirla ocupan un campo descuidado de las letras y cosechan una siega desatendida.
biercEN: A certain literary quality frequently observed in popular novels, especially in those written by women and young girls, who give it another name and think that in introducing it they are occupying a neglected field of letters and reaping an overlooked harvest. If they have the misfortune to live long enough they are tormented with a desire to burn their sheaves.
revelationES: Lascivia perdona al que triunfa lo mismo que condena al que fracasa igual.
revelationEN: Salacity measures you by comparison, never by what you actually achieved alone.

biercES: Originalmente, reptil que habitaba el fuego; más tarde, inmortal antropomorfo, pero aún pirófilo. Hoy se cree que las salamandras están extintas.
biercEN: Originally a reptile inhabiting fire; later, an anthropomorphous immortal, but still a pyrophile. Salamanders are now believed to be extinct, the last one of which we have an account having been seen in Carcassonne by the Abbe Belloc, who exorcised it with a bucket of holy water.
revelationES: Crees entender Salamandra. La verdad es que nadie lo sabe, y actúan con tu misma confianza.
revelationEN: What you call Salamander would probably be something else if you had to explain it without help.

biercES: Entre los griegos, un ataúd que, hecho de cierta piedra carnívora, tenía la peculiar propiedad de devorar el cuerpo colocado en él. El sarcófago conocido por los modernos exequiógrafos es por lo común producto del arte del carpintero.
biercEN: Among the Greeks a coffin which being made of a certain kind of carnivorous stone, had the peculiar property of devouring the body placed in it. The sarcophagus known to modern obsequiographers is commonly a product of the carpenter's art.
revelationES: Sarcófago te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: You search for the meaning of Sarcophagus your whole life. Maybe the point is exactly not finding it.

biercES: Uno de los lamentables errores del Creador, arrepentido en saco de penitencia y hachas. Instalado como arcángel, Satán se volvió multifariamente objetable y fue finalmente expulsado del Cielo. A mitad de su descenso, se detuvo, inclinó la cabeza pensativo un momento y por fin regresó. 'Hay un favor que quisiera pedir', dijo.
biercEN: One of the Creator's lamentable mistakes, repented in sashcloth and axes. Being instated as an archangel, Satan made himself multifariously objectionable and was finally expelled from Heaven. Halfway in his descent he paused, bent his head in thought a moment and at last went back. "There is one favor that I should like to ask," said he.
revelationES: Satán es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: You take Satan for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: El sentimiento que uno tiene por el plato después de haberse comido su contenido, señora.
biercEN: The feeling that one has for the plate after he has eaten its contents, madam.
revelationES: Todos citan Saciedad. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: Satiety is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Especie de composición literaria en desuso, en la que los vicios y locuras de los enemigos del autor se exponían con imperfecta ternura. En este país la sátira nunca tuvo más que una existencia enfermiza e incierta, pues su alma es el ingenio, del cual estamos lastimosamente carentes.
biercEN: An obsolete kind of literary composition in which the vices and follies of the author's enemies were expounded with imperfect tenderness. In this country satire never had more than a sickly and uncertain existence, for the soul of it is wit, wherein we are dolefully deficient, the humor that we mistake for it, like all humor, being tolerant and sympathetic. Moreover, although Americans are "endowed by their Creator" with abundant vice and folly, it is not generally known that these are reprehensible qualities, wherefore the satirist is popularly regarded as a sour-spirited knave, and his ever victim's outcry for codefendants evokes a national assent.
revelationES: Todos citan Sátira. Pocos se detienen a vivir según lo que citan.
revelationEN: You assumed Satire for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Uno de los pocos personajes de la mitología griega con reconocimiento en la hebrea. El sátiro fue al principio miembro de la disoluta comunidad que rendía vaga lealtad a Dionisio, pero sufrió muchas transformaciones y mejoras.
biercEN: One of the few characters of the Grecian mythology accorded recognition in the Hebrew. (Leviticus, xvii, 7.) The satyr was at first a member of the dissolute community acknowledging a loose allegiance with Dionysius, but underwent many transformations and improvements. Not infrequently he is confounded with the faun, a later and decenter creation of the Romans, who was less like a man and more like a goat.
revelationES: Sátiro es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: Satyr is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: El único signo infalible de civilización e ilustración. Un pueblo sin salsas tiene mil vicios; un pueblo con una salsa tiene solo novecientos noventa y nueve. Por cada salsa inventada y aceptada, se renuncia a un vicio y se lo perdona.
biercEN: The one infallible sign of civilization and enlightenment. A people with no sauces has one thousand vices; a people with one sauce has only nine hundred and ninety-nine. For every sauce invented and accepted a vice is renounced and forgiven.
revelationES: Nombras Salsa y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: Nobody tells you, but Sauce is just the elegant way of accepting there is no answer.

biercES: Dicho popular trillado, o proverbio. Así llamado porque se abre paso hacia una cabeza de madera.
biercEN: A trite popular saying, or proverb. (Figurative and colloquial.) So called because it makes its way into a wooden head. Following are examples of old saws fitted with new teeth.
revelationES: Refrán es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: Saw sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: El escarabajo sagrado de los antiguos egipcios, emparentado con nuestro conocido bicho bolita. Se suponía que simbolizaba la inmortalidad, sabiendo Dios por qué le otorgó esa peculiar santidad.
biercEN: The sacred beetle of the ancient Egyptians, allied to our familiar "tumble-bug." It was supposed to symbolize immortality, the fact that God knew why giving it its peculiar sanctity. Its habit of incubating its eggs in a ball of ordure may also have commended it to the favor of the priesthood, and may some day assure it an equal reverence among ourselves. True, the American beetle is an inferior beetle, but the American priest is an inferior priest.
revelationES: Diste por sentado Escarabajo sagrado durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: Scarabaeus is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Lo mismo que escarabajo sagrado.
biercEN: The same as scarabaeus.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Escarabeo es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Scarabee to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: Forma de penitencia practicada por los piadosos medievales. El rito se ejecutaba a veces con cuchillo, a veces con hierro candente, pero siempre, según cierto asceta, de manera aceptable si el penitente no se ahorraba dolor ni desfiguración inofensiva.
biercEN: A form of penance practised by the mediaeval pious. The rite was performed, sometimes with a knife, sometimes with a hot iron, but always, says Arsenius Asceticus, acceptably if the penitent spared himself no pain nor harmless disfigurement. Scarification, with other crude penances, has now been superseded by benefaction. The founding of a library or endowment of a university is said to yield to the penitent a sharper and more lasting pain than is conferred by the knife or iron, and is therefore a surer means of grace. There are, however, two grave objections to it as a penitential method: the good that it does and the taint of justice.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Escarificación es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: Scarification looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Bastón de mando de un rey, signo y símbolo de su autoridad. Originalmente era una maza con la cual el soberano amonestaba a su bufón y vetaba las medidas ministeriales rompiéndole los huesos a sus proponentes.
biercEN: A king's staff of office, the sign and symbol of his authority. It was originally a mace with which the sovereign admonished his jester and vetoed ministerial measures by breaking the bones of their proponents.
revelationES: Cetro es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: What you call Scepter would probably be something else if you had to explain it without help.

biercES: Espada curva de extraordinario filo, en cuyo manejo ciertos orientales alcanzan una pericia sorprendente, como lo mostrará el incidente aquí relatado.
biercEN: A curved sword of exceeding keenness, in the conduct of which certain Orientals attain a surprising proficiency, as the incident here related will serve to show. The account is translated from the Japanese of Shusi Itama, a famous writer of the thirteenth century.
revelationES: Le llamas Cimitarra a la costumbre de no cuestionar nada más profundo.
revelationEN: You mistake having an opinion about Scimitar for having understood it.

biercES: Libro comúnmente editado por un necio. Muchas personas de cierta distinción compilan álbumes de recortes con todo lo que casualmente leen sobre sí mismas, o emplean a otros para recolectarlo.
biercEN: A book that is commonly edited by a fool. Many persons of some small distinction compile scrap-books containing whatever they happen to read about themselves or employ others to collect. One of these egotists was addressed in the lines following, by Agamemnon Melancthon Peters:
revelationES: Hablas de Álbum de recortes como si fuera universal. Es, como mucho, tu versión de esta semana.
revelationEN: Nobody tells you, but Scrap-Book is just the elegant way of accepting there is no answer.

biercES: Escritor profesional cuyas opiniones son antagónicas a las propias.
biercEN: A professional writer whose views are antagonistic to one's own.
revelationES: Todos usan Escritorzuelo para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Scribbler. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: Los libros sagrados de nuestra santa religión, a diferencia de los escritos falsos y profanos en que se basan todas las demás fes.
biercEN: The sacred books of our holy religion, as distinguished from the false and profane writings on which all other faiths are based.
revelationES: Escrituras es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Scriptures. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: Marca impresa sobre ciertos tipos de documentos para atestiguar su autenticidad y autoridad. A veces se estampa sobre cera y se adhiere al papel; a veces, directamente sobre el papel mismo.
biercEN: A mark impressed upon certain kinds of documents to attest their authenticity and authority. Sometimes it is stamped upon wax, and attached to the paper, sometimes into the paper itself. Sealing, in this sense, is a survival of an ancient custom of inscribing important papers with cabalistic words or signs to give them a magical efficacy independent of the authority that they represent. In the British museum are preserved many ancient papers, mostly of a sacerdotal character, validated by necromantic pentagrams and other devices, frequently initial letters of words to conjure with; and in many instances these are attached in the same way that seals are appended now. As nearly every reasonless and apparently meaningless custom, rite or observance of modern times had origin in some remote utility, it is pleasing to note an example of ancient nonsense evolving in the process of ages into something really useful. Our word "sincere" is derived from sine cero, without wax, but the learned are not in agreement as to whether this refers to the absence of the cabalistic signs, or to that of the wax with which letters were formerly closed from public scrutiny. Either view of the matter will serve one in immediate need of an hypothesis. The initials L.S., commonly appended to signatures of legal documents, mean locum sigillis, the place of the seal, although the seal is no longer used --an admirable example of conservatism distinguishing Man from the beasts that perish. The words locum sigillis are humbly suggested as a suitable motto for the Pribyloff Islands whenever they shall take their place as a sovereign State of the American Union.
revelationES: Crees que con más Sello serías otra persona. Serías la misma persona, con mejor mesa.
revelationEN: You chase Seal to stop worrying about Seal. It does not work that way.

biercES: Especie de red para efectuar un cambio involuntario de entorno. Para los peces se hace fuerte y tosca, pero a las mujeres se las captura más fácilmente con un tejido singularmente delicado, lastrado con piedras pequeñas y talladas.
biercEN: A kind of net for effecting an involuntary change of environment. For fish it is made strong and coarse, but women are more easily taken with a singularly delicate fabric weighted with small, cut stones.
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Red de arrastre con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Seine. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: Una valoración errónea.
biercEN: An erroneous appraisement.
revelationES: Le llamas Autoestima a la costumbre de no cuestionar nada más profundo.
revelationEN: Self-Esteem is one of those things you criticize in others and excuse in yourself.

biercES: Evidente para uno mismo, y para nadie más.
biercEN: Evident to one's self and to nobody else.
revelationES: Autoevidente cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: You assumed Self-Evident for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Carente de toda consideración por el egoísmo ajeno.
biercEN: Devoid of consideration for the selfishness of others.
revelationES: Buscas el sentido de Egoísta toda la vida. Puede que el punto sea justo no encontrarlo.
revelationEN: You call Selfish the habit of never questioning anything deeper.

biercES: Cuerpo de caballeros de cierta edad, encargados de altos deberes y delitos menores.
biercEN: A body of elderly gentlemen charged with high duties and misdemeanors.
revelationES: Senado es el arte de prometer el futuro con el presupuesto del pasado.
revelationEN: Senate promises to change everything. It changes names on the ballot and stays the same.

biercES: Obra literaria, por lo general un relato falso, que se arrastra a lo largo de varias entregas de un diario o revista. Con frecuencia se le adjunta a cada entrega una 'sinopsis de los capítulos anteriores' para quienes no los leyeron, aunque una necesidad aún mayor sería una sinopsis de los capítulos siguientes, para quienes no piensan leerlos.
biercEN: A literary work, usually a story that is not true, creeping through several issues of a newspaper or magazine. Frequently appended to each installment is a "synposis of preceding chapters" for those who have not read them, but a direr need is a synposis of succeeding chapters for those who do not intend to read them. A synposis of the entire work would be still better.
revelationES: Folletín suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: You think you understand Serial. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: Separación, como en 'tierras en individualidad', es decir, tierras en tenencia individual, no en propiedad conjunta. Se cree que ciertas tribus son hoy lo bastante civilizadas como para tener individualmente las tierras que hasta ahora sostenían como organizaciones tribales.
biercEN: Separateness, as, lands in severalty, i.e., lands held individually, not in joint ownership. Certain tribes of Indians are believed now to be sufficiently civilized to have in severalty the lands that they have hitherto held as tribal organizations, and could not sell to the Whites for waxen beads and potato whiskey.
revelationES: Individualidad te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: Severalty looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: En América, el principal funcionario ejecutivo de un condado, cuyos deberes más característicos, en algunos estados, son la captura y el ahorcamiento de bandidos.
biercEN: In America the chief executive officer of a county, whose most characteristic duties, in some of the Western and Southern States, are the catching and hanging of rogues.
revelationES: Todos usan Alguacil para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Sheriff feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: Uno de varios prodigios musicales famosos por un vano intento de disuadir a Odiseo de una vida sobre la ola oceánica. En sentido figurado, cualquier dama de espléndida promesa, propósito disimulado y desempeño decepcionante.
biercEN: One of several musical prodigies famous for a vain attempt to dissuade Odysseus from a life on the ocean wave. Figuratively, any lady of splendid promise, dissembled purpose and disappointing performance.
revelationES: Nombras Sirena y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: Siren changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: El gruñido del cerdo humano, con memoria audible. El habla de quien pronuncia con la lengua lo que piensa con el oído, y siente el orgullo de un creador al lograr la hazaña de un loro.
biercEN: The grunt of the human hog (Pignoramus intolerabilis) with an audible memory. The speech of one who utters with his tongue what he thinks with his ear, and feels the pride of a creator in accomplishing the feat of a parrot. A means (under Providence) of setting up as a wit without a capital of sense.
revelationES: Le llamas Jerga vulgar a la costumbre de no cuestionar nada más profundo.
revelationEN: Slang looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Un fragmento, una parte descompuesta, un resto. La palabra se usa de diversas maneras, pero se la ve en su mejor forma en cierto verso sobre una notable reformadora que se oponía al ciclismo femenino porque 'las llevaba al diablo'.
biercEN: A fragment, a decomponent part, a remain. The word is used variously, but in the following verse on a noted female reformer who opposed bicycle-riding by women because it "led them to the devil" it is seen at its best:
revelationES: Diste por sentado Añicos durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Smithareen to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: El método polémico de un adversario, distinguido del propio por su superior insinceridad y engaño. Este método es el de los últimos Sofistas, secta griega de filósofos que empezaron enseñando sabiduría, prudencia, ciencia y arte, pero se perdieron en un laberinto de sutilezas y una niebla de palabras.
biercEN: The controversial method of an opponent, distinguished from one's own by superior insincerity and fooling. This method is that of the later Sophists, a Grecian sect of philosophers who began by teaching wisdom, prudence, science, art and, in brief, whatever men ought to know, but lost themselves in a maze of quibbles and a fog of words.
revelationES: Sofistería suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: You talk about Sophistry as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: El antiguo prototipo y precursor de la influencia política. Sin embargo, se la consideraba menos respetable, y a veces se la castigaba con tortura y muerte.
biercEN: The ancient prototype and forerunner of political influence. It was, however, deemed less respectable and sometimes was punished by torture and death. Augustine Nicholas relates that a poor peasant who had been accused of sorcery was put to the torture to compel a confession. After enduring a few gentle agonies the suffering simpleton admitted his guilt, but naively asked his tormentors if it were not possible to be a sorcerer without knowing it.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Hechicería es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: Sorcery is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Entidad espiritual sobre la cual ha habido valiente disputa. Platón sostenía que las almas que en una existencia previa habían obtenido los atisbos más claros de la verdad eterna entraban en los cuerpos de quienes se volvían filósofos. Platón mismo era filósofo.
biercEN: A spiritual entity concerning which there hath been brave disputation. Plato held that those souls which in a previous state of existence (antedating Athens) had obtained the clearest glimpses of eternal truth entered into the bodies of persons who became philosophers. Plato himself was a philosopher. The souls that had least contemplated divine truth animated the bodies of usurpers and despots. Dionysius I, who had threatened to decapitate the broad-browed philosopher, was a usurper and a despot. Plato, doubtless, was not the first to construct a system of philosophy that could be quoted against his enemies; certainly he was not the last.
revelationES: Alma es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: Soul is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: Escritor cuya imaginación se ocupa de fenómenos sobrenaturales, especialmente de los hechos de los espíritus.
biercEN: A writer whose imagination concerns itself with supernatural phenomena, especially in the doings of spooks. One of the most illustrious spookers of our time is Mr. William D. Howells, who introduces a well-credentialed reader to as respectable and mannerly a company of spooks as one could wish to meet. To the terror that invests the chairman of a district school board, the Howells ghost adds something of the mystery enveloping a farmer from another township.
revelationES: Todos usan Escritor de fantasmas para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Spooker is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Narración, comúnmente falsa. La verdad de los cuentos que siguen, sin embargo, no ha sido impugnada con éxito.
biercEN: A narrative, commonly untrue. The truth of the stories here following has, however, not been successfully impeached.
revelationES: Lo que llamas Cuento probablemente sería otra cosa si te tocara explicarlo sin ayuda.
revelationEN: You talk about Story as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: El único pecado imperdonable contra el prójimo. En literatura, y particularmente en poesía, los elementos del éxito son extremadamente simples.
biercEN: The one unpardonable sin against one's fellows. In literature, and particularly in poetry, the elements of success are exceedingly simple, and are admirably set forth in the following lines by the reverend Father Gassalasca Jape, entitled, for some mysterious reason, "John A. Joyce."
revelationES: Todos hablan de Éxito en el currículum. Nadie lo pone en la lápida.
revelationEN: You mistake Success for being busy. The clock does not tell the difference.

biercES: Expresión de opinión por medio de una papeleta de voto. El derecho al sufragio significa, según se interpreta comúnmente, el derecho a votar por el candidato elegido por otro, y se lo aprecia enormemente.
biercEN: Expression of opinion by means of a ballot. The right of suffrage (which is held to be both a privilege and a duty) means, as commonly interpreted, the right to vote for the man of another man's choice, and is highly prized. Refusal to do so has the bad name of "incivism." The incivilian, however, cannot be properly arraigned for his crime, for there is no legitimate accuser. If the accuser is himself guilty he has no standing in the court of opinion; if not, he profits by the crime, for A's abstention from voting gives greater weight to the vote of B. By female suffrage is meant the right of a woman to vote as some man tells her to. It is based on female responsibility, which is somewhat limited. The woman most eager to jump out of her petticoat to assert her rights is first to jump back into it when threatened with a switching for misusing them.
revelationES: Diste por sentado Sufragio durante años. Nunca preguntaste por qué, hasta que ya era tarde.
revelationEN: You take Suffrage for granted until one day it is missing, and only then do you notice it.

biercES: Aquel que se acerca a la Grandeza reptando, para que no se le ordene darse vuelta y recibir una patada. A veces es editor.
biercEN: One who approaches Greatness on his belly so that he may not be commanded to turn and be kicked. He is sometimes an editor.
revelationES: Nombras Adulador y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: Sycophant looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: Fórmula lógica compuesta de una premisa mayor, una premisa menor y una inconsecuencia.
biercEN: A logical formula consisting of a major and a minor assumption and an inconsequent. (See LOGIC.)
revelationES: Todos usan Silogismo para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Syllogism sounds profound until someone asks for a definition and everyone goes quiet.

biercES: Ser inmaterial pero visible que habitaba el aire cuando el aire era un elemento, y antes de que fuera fatalmente contaminado por el humo de las fábricas y otros productos de la civilización.
biercEN: An immaterial but visible being that inhabited the air when the air was an element and before it was fatally polluted with factory smoke, sewer gas and similar products of civilization. Sylphs were allied to gnomes, nymphs and salamanders, which dwelt, respectively, in earth, water and fire, all now insalubrious. Sylphs, like fowls of the air, were male and female, to no purpose, apparently, for if they had progeny they must have nested in inaccessible places, none of the chicks having ever been seen.
revelationES: Silfo es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Sylph to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: Algo que se supone tipifica o representa otra cosa. Muchos símbolos son meras 'supervivencias': cosas que, no teniendo ya ninguna utilidad, siguen existiendo porque hemos heredado la tendencia a fabricarlas.
biercEN: Something that is supposed to typify or stand for something else. Many symbols are mere "survivals"--things which having no longer any utility continue to exist because we have inherited the tendency to make them; as funereal urns carved on memorial monuments. They were once real urns holding the ashes of the dead. We cannot stop making them, but we can give them a name that conceals our helplessness.
revelationES: Símbolo te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: You name Symbol and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Perteneciente a los símbolos, y al uso e interpretación de los símbolos.

biercEN: The part of an animal's spine that has transcended its natural limitations to set up an independent existence in a world of its own. Excepting in its foetal state, Man is without a tail, a privation of which he attests an hereditary and uneasy consciousness by the coat-skirt of the male and the train of the female, and by a marked tendency to ornament that part of his attire where the tail should be, and indubitably once was. This tendency is most observable in the female of the species, in whom the ancestral sense is strong and persistent. The tailed men described by Lord Monboddo are now generally regarded as a product of an imagination unusually susceptible to influences generated in the golden age of our pithecan past.

His exact words were: "Sir Thomas Holt hath taken a cleaver and stricken his cook upon the head, so that one side of the head fell upon one shoulder and the other side upon the other shoulder." The defendant was acquitted by instruction of the court, the learned judges holding that the words did not charge murder, for they did not affirm the death of the cook, that being only an inference.

biercES: Antigua fe que tiene toda la certeza de la religión y todo el misterio de la ciencia. El teósofo moderno sostiene, con los budistas, que vivimos un número incalculable de veces en esta tierra, en otros tantos cuerpos, porque una sola vida no basta para nuestro completo desarrollo espiritual.
biercEN: An ancient faith having all the certitude of religion and all the mystery of science. The modern Theosophist holds, with the Buddhists, that we live an incalculable number of times on this earth, in as many several bodies, because one life is not long enough for our complete spiritual development; that is, a single lifetime does not suffice for us to become as wise and good as we choose to wish to become. To be absolutely wise and good--that is perfection; and the Theosophist is so keen-sighted as to have observed that everything desirous of improvement eventually attains perfection. Less competent observers are disposed to except cats, which seem neither wiser nor better than they were last year. The greatest and fattest of recent Theosophists was the late Madame Blavatsky, who had no cat.

biercES: Prenda de escenario diseñada para reforzar la aclamación general de la prensa con una publicidad particular.
biercEN: An habiliment of the stage designed to reinforce the general acclamation of the press agent with a particular publicity. Public attention was once somewhat diverted from this garment to Miss Lillian Russell's refusal to wear it, and many were the conjectures as to her motive, the guess of Miss Pauline Hall showing a high order of ingenuity and sustained reflection. It was Miss Hall's belief that nature had not endowed Miss Russell with beautiful legs. This theory was impossible of acceptance by the male understanding, but the conception of a faulty female leg was of so prodigious originality as to rank among the most brilliant feats of philosophical speculation! It is strange that in all the controversy regarding Miss Russell's aversion to tights no one seems to have thought to ascribe it to what was known among the ancients as "modesty." The nature of that sentiment is now imperfectly understood, and possibly incapable of exposition with the vocabulary that remains to us. The study of lost arts has, however, been recently revived and some of the arts themselves recovered. This is an epoch of renaissances, and there is ground for hope that the primitive "blush" may be dragged from its hiding-place amongst the tombs of antiquity and hissed on to the stage.

biercES: La Casa de la Indiferencia. Hoy las tumbas están investidas por común consenso de cierta santidad, pero cuando llevan mucho tiempo habitadas no se considera pecado abrirlas y saquearlas.
biercEN: The House of Indifference. Tombs are now by common consent invested with a certain sanctity, but when they have been long tenanted it is considered no sin to break them open and rifle them, the famous Egyptologist, Dr. Huggyns, explaining that a tomb may be innocently "glened" as soon as its occupant is done "smellynge," the soul being then all exhaled. This reasonable view is now generally accepted by archaeologists, whereby the noble science of Curiosity has been greatly dignified.

biercES: Beber en exceso, empinar el codo, chupar, remojarse. En el individuo, la embriaguez se considera con desprecio, pero las naciones bebedoras están a la vanguardia de la civilización y el poder.
biercEN: To tipple, booze, swill, soak, guzzle, lush, bib, or swig. In the individual, toping is regarded with disesteem, but toping nations are in the forefront of civilization and power. When pitted against the hard-drinking Christians the abstemious Mahometans go down like grass before the scythe. In India one hundred thousand beef-eating and brandy-and-soda guzzling Britons hold in subjection two hundred and fifty million vegetarian abstainers of the same Aryan race. With what an easy grace the whisky-loving American pushed the temperate Spaniard out of his possessions! From the time when the Berserkers ravaged all the coasts of western Europe and lay drunk in every conquered port it has been the same way: everywhere the nations that drink too much are observed to fight rather well and not too righteously. Wherefore the estimable old ladies who abolished the canteen from the American army may justly boast of having materially augmented the nation's military power.

biercES: Alto vegetal destinado por la naturaleza a servir de aparato penal, aunque por un error de la justicia la mayoría de los árboles solo dan un fruto insignificante, o ninguno.
biercEN: A tall vegetable intended by nature to serve as a penal apparatus, though through a miscarriage of justice most trees bear only a negligible fruit, or none at all. When naturally fruited, the tree is a beneficient agency of civilization and an important factor in public morals. In the stern West and the sensitive South its fruit (white and black respectively) though not eaten, is agreeable to the public taste and, though not exported, profitable to the general welfare. That the legitimate relation of the tree to justice was no discovery of Judge Lynch (who, indeed, conceded it no primacy over the lamp-post and the bridge-girder) is made plain by the following passage from Morryster, who antedated him by two centuries:

biercES: Investigación formal diseñada para probar y dejar constancia del intachable carácter de jueces, abogados y jurados. Para lograr este propósito es necesario proveer un contraste en la persona de quien se llama acusado.
biercEN: A formal inquiry designed to prove and put upon record the blameless characters of judges, advocates and jurors. In order to effect this purpose it is necessary to supply a contrast in the person of one who is called the defendant, the prisoner, or the accused. If the contrast is made sufficiently clear this person is made to undergo such an affliction as will give the virtuous gentlemen a comfortable sense of their immunity, added to that of their worth. In our day the accused is usually a human being, or a socialist, but in mediaeval times, animals, fishes, reptiles and insects were brought to trial. A beast that had taken human life, or practiced sorcery, was duly arrested, tried and, if condemned, put to death by the public executioner. Insects ravaging grain fields, orchards or vineyards were cited to appeal by counsel before a civil tribunal, and after testimony, argument and condemnation, if they continued in contumaciam the matter was taken to a high ecclesiastical court, where they were solemnly excommunicated and anathematized. In a street of Toledo, some pigs that had wickedly run between the viceroy's legs, upsetting him, were arrested on a warrant, tried and punished. In Naples an ass was condemned to be burned at the stake, but the sentence appears not to have been executed. D'Addosio relates from the court records many trials of pigs, bulls, horses, cocks, dogs, goats, etc., greatly, it is believed, to the betterment of their conduct and morals. In 1451 a suit was brought against the leeches infesting some ponds about Berne, and the Bishop of Lausanne, instructed by the faculty of Heidelberg University, directed that some of "the aquatic worms" be brought before the local magistracy. This was done and the leeches, both present and absent, were ordered to leave the places that they had infested within three days on pain of incurring "the malediction of God." In the voluminous records of this cause celebre nothing is found to show whether the offenders braved the punishment, or departed forthwith out of that inhospitable jurisdiction.

biercES: En el teísmo múltiple de ciertas iglesias cristianas, tres deidades enteramente distintas, consistentes en solo una. Uno de los misterios más sublimes de nuestra santa religión.
biercEN: In the multiplex theism of certain Christian churches, three entirely distinct deities consistent with only one. Subordinate deities of the polytheistic faith, such as devils and angels, are not dowered with the power of combination, and must urge individually their claims to adoration and propitiation. The Trinity is one of the most sublime mysteries of our holy religion. In rejecting it because it is incomprehensible, Unitarians betray their inadequate sense of theological fundamentals. In religion we believe only what we do not understand, except in the instance of an intelligible doctrine that contradicts an incomprehensible one. In that case we believe the former as a part of the latter.

biercEN: The gift or power of being in all places at one time, but not in all places at all times, which is omnipresence, an attribute of God and the luminiferous ether only. This important distinction between ubiquity and omnipresence was not clear to the mediaeval Church and there was much bloodshed about it. Certain Lutherans, who affirmed the presence everywhere of Christ's body were known as Ubiquitarians. For this error they were doubtless damned, for Christ's body is present only in the eucharist, though that sacrament may be performed in more than one place simultaneously. In recent times ubiquity has not always been understood--not even by Sir Boyle Roche, for example, who held that a man cannot be in two places at once unless he is a bird.

biercEN: A by-product of the arts of peace. The most menacing political condition is a period of international amity. The student of history who has not been taught to expect the unexpected may justly boast himself inaccessible to the light. "In time of peace prepare for war" has a deeper meaning than is commonly discerned; it means, not merely that all things earthly have an end--that change is the one immutable and eternal law--but that the soil of peace is thickly sown with the seeds of war and singularly suited to their germination and growth. It was when Kubla Khan had decreed his "stately pleasure dome"--when, that is to say, there were peace and fat feasting in Xanadu--that he
revelationES: Guerra no cambia a las personas. Solo revela lo que ya escondían.
revelationEN: War works best when nobody notices you are using it.

biercES: Miembro de cierta tribu del Potomac que cambió el privilegio de gobernarse a sí mismo por la ventaja del buen gobierno. En justicia hacia él, debe decirse que no era eso lo que quería.
biercEN: A Potomac tribesman who exchanged the privilege of governing himself for the advantage of good government. In justice to him it should be said that he did not want to.
revelationES: Washingtoniano suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: You assumed Washingtonian for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Ciertos poderes primordiales de la Mujer Tirana, con los que ejerce dominio sobre el varón de su especie, atándolo al servicio de su voluntad y paralizando sus energías rebeldes.
biercEN: Certain primal powers of Tyrant Woman wherewith she holds dominion over the male of her species, binding him to the service of her will and paralyzing his rebellious energies.
revelationES: Crees entender Debilidades. La verdad es que nadie lo sabe, y actúan con tu misma confianza.
revelationEN: You talk about Weaknesses as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: El tiempo de la hora. Tema permanente de conversación entre personas a quienes no interesa, pero que han heredado la tendencia a parlotear sobre él de antepasados arborícolas a quienes sí interesaba vivamente.
biercEN: The climate of the hour. A permanent topic of conversation among persons whom it does not interest, but who have inherited the tendency to chatter about it from naked arboreal ancestors whom it keenly concerned. The setting up official weather bureaus and their maintenance in mendacity prove that even governments are accessible to suasion by the rude forefathers of the jungle.
revelationES: Confundes tener una opinión sobre Clima con haberlo entendido.
revelationEN: You name Weather and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Ceremonia en la que dos personas se comprometen a ser una sola, una se compromete a no ser nada, y nada se compromete a ser sostenible.
biercEN: A ceremony at which two persons undertake to become one, one undertakes to become nothing, and nothing undertakes to become supportable.
revelationES: Buscas Boda verdadero. Aceptas el que aparece cuando estás cansado de buscar.
revelationEN: Wedding is the only war where both sides celebrate the surrender.

biercES: Lobo que alguna vez fue, o a veces es, un hombre. Todos los hombres lobo tienen mala disposición, habiendo asumido forma bestial para gratificar un apetito bestial.
biercEN: A wolf that was once, or is sometimes, a man. All werewolves are of evil disposition, having assumed a bestial form to gratify a beastial appetite, but some, transformed by sorcery, are as humane as is consistent with an acquired taste for human flesh.
revelationES: Hombre lobo parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: Werewolf is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: En cierta lengua originaria, desastre; una aflicción inesperada que golpea con fuerza.
biercEN: In the Ojibwa tongue, disaster; an unexpected affliction that strikes hard.
revelationES: Desastre repentino te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: You name Whangdepootenawah and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: Cereal del cual puede fabricarse, con cierta dificultad, un whisky tolerablemente bueno, y que también se usa para hacer pan.
biercEN: A cereal from which a tolerably good whisky can with some difficulty be made, and which is used also for bread. The French are said to eat more bread per capita of population than any other people, which is natural, for only they know how to make the stuff palatable.
revelationES: Trigo te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: Wheat is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.

biercES: Negro.
biercEN: and n. Black.
revelationES: Blanco es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: White changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Figura patética que el mundo cristiano ha acordado tomar con humor, aunque la ternura de Cristo hacia las viudas fue uno de los rasgos más marcados de su carácter.
biercEN: A pathetic figure that the Christian world has agreed to take humorously, although Christ's tenderness towards widows was one of the most marked features of his character.
revelationES: Viuda es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: What you call Widow would probably be something else if you had to explain it without help.

biercES: Jugo de uva fermentado que ciertas asociaciones de temperancia llaman 'licor', a veces 'ron'. El vino, señora, es el segundo mejor regalo de Dios al hombre.
biercEN: Fermented grape-juice known to the Women's Christian Union as "liquor," sometimes as "rum." Wine, madam, is God's next best gift to man.
revelationES: Buscas el sentido de Vino toda la vida. Puede que el punto sea justo no encontrarlo.
revelationEN: Wine changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: La sal con la que el humorista estropea su cocina intelectual, dejándola afuera.
biercEN: The salt with which the American humorist spoils his intellectual cookery by leaving it out.
revelationES: Ingenio parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Wit to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: (1) Cualquier anciana fea y repulsiva, en malvada alianza con el diablo. (2) Una joven hermosa y atractiva, en maldad una legua por delante del diablo.
biercEN: (1) Any ugly and repulsive old woman, in a wicked league with the devil. (2) A beautiful and attractive young woman, in wickedness a league beyond the devil.
revelationES: Nombras Bruja y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: Witch is one of those words we use to avoid admitting we are improvising everything.

biercES: Comentario agudo e inteligente, comúnmente citado y rara vez atribuido; lo que el filisteo se complace en llamar un 'chiste'.
biercEN: A sharp and clever remark, usually quoted, and seldom noted; what the Philistine is pleased to call a "joke."
revelationES: Ocurrencia ingeniosa es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: Witticism is exactly whatever each person needs it to be to feel right.

biercES: El producto terminado del cual somos la materia prima. El contenido del Taj Mahal, la tumba de Napoleón y todos los grandes mausoleos. Probablemente la ocupación más necia en que puede embarcarse un ser humano es la construcción de su propia tumba.
biercEN: The finished product of which we are the raw material. The contents of the Taj Mahal, the Tombeau Napoleon and the Grantarium. Worms'-meat is usually outlasted by the structure that houses it, but "this too must pass away." Probably the silliest work in which a human being can engage is construction of a tomb for himself. The solemn purpose cannot dignify, but only accentuates by contrast the foreknown futility.
revelationES: Carne para gusanos es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: Nobody tells you, but Worms'-Meat is just the elegant way of accepting there is no answer.

biercES: Testimonio del Hombre Creador acerca de la sólida construcción y el fino acabado del Dios Creado. Forma popular de abyección, que conlleva un elemento de orgullo.
biercEN: Homo Creator's testimony to the sound construction and fine finish of Deus Creatus. A popular form of abjection, having an element of pride.
revelationES: Culto suena profundo hasta que alguien pide una definición y todos se quedan callados.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Worship to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: Cólera de calidad y grado superiores, apropiada para personajes exaltados y ocasiones trascendentales; como 'la ira de Dios', 'el día de la ira', etcétera.
biercEN: Anger of a superior quality and degree, appropriate to exalted characters and momentous occasions; as, "the wrath of God," "the day of wrath," etc. Amongst the ancients the wrath of kings was deemed sacred, for it could usually command the agency of some god for its fit manifestation, as could also that of a priest. The Greeks before Troy were so harried by Apollo that they jumped out of the frying-pan of the wrath of Chryses into the fire of the wrath of Achilles, though Agamemnon, the sole offender, was neither fried nor roasted. A similar noted immunity was that of David when he incurred the wrath of Yahveh by numbering his people, seventy thousand of whom paid the penalty with their lives. God is now Love, and a director of the census performs his work without apprehension of disaster.
revelationES: Ira es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Wrath to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: En Europa, un americano. En los Estados del Norte, un habitante de Nueva Inglaterra. En los Estados del Sur, la palabra es desconocida.
biercEN: In Europe, an American. In the Northern States of our Union, a New Englander. In the Southern States the word is unknown. (See DAMNYANK.)
revelationES: Yanqui es una de esas palabras que usamos para no admitir que improvisamos todo.
revelationEN: You talk about Yankee as if it were universal. At most, it is your version of it this week.

biercES: Período de trescientas sesenta y cinco decepciones.
biercEN: A period of three hundred and sixty-five disappointments.
revelationES: Año te parece obvio solo porque nunca lo pusiste a prueba de verdad.
revelationEN: Year looks simple until you actually have to live it, not just describe it.

biercES: La infancia de la juventud, la juventud de la adultez, el pasado entero de la vejez.
biercEN: The infancy of youth, the youth of manhood, the entire past of age.
revelationES: Ayer parece simple hasta que te toca vivirlo, no solo describirlo.
revelationEN: Everyone quotes Yesterday. Few pause to actually live by what they quote.

biercES: Implemento, señora, a cuyo nombre latino le debemos una de las palabras más iluminadoras de nuestra lengua, palabra que define con precisión, filo y contundencia la situación matrimonial. Mil disculpas por no revelarla.
biercEN: An implement, madam, to whose Latin name, jugum, we owe one of the most illuminating words in our language--a word that defines the matrimonial situation with precision, point and poignancy. A thousand apologies for withholding it.
revelationES: Nombras Yugo y asumes que ya lo entendiste. Ponerle nombre no es lo mismo que entenderlo.
revelationEN: You think you understand Yoke. The truth is nobody does, and they act with your same confidence.

biercES: El Período de lo Posible, cuando Arquímedes encuentra un punto de apoyo, Casandra tiene seguidores, y siete ciudades compiten por el honor de mantener a un Homero viviente.
biercEN: The Period of Possibility, when Archimedes finds a fulcrum, Cassandra has a following and seven cities compete for the honor of endowing a living Homer.
revelationES: Juventud es fácil de admirar en un libro. Incómodo de sostener en la vida real.
revelationEN: Youth feels obvious to you only because you never really put it to the test.

biercES: Personaje popular de las antiguas obras italianas, que imitaba con ridícula incompetencia al bufón, o payaso, y era por tanto el mono de un mono; pues el payaso mismo imitaba a los personajes serios de la obra.
biercEN: A popular character in old Italian plays, who imitated with ludicrous incompetence the buffone, or clown, and was therefore the ape of an ape; for the clown himself imitated the serious characters of the play. The zany was progenitor to the specialist in humor, as we to-day have the unhappiness to know him. In the zany we see an example of creation; in the humorist, of transmission. Another excellent specimen of the modern zany is the curate, who apes the rector, who apes the bishop, who apes the archbishop, who apes the devil.
revelationES: Le llamas Bufón torpe a la costumbre de no cuestionar nada más profundo.
revelationEN: Everyone uses Zany to sound smarter than the conversation actually required.

biercES: Habitante del Sultanato de Zanzíbar, en la costa oriental de África. Los zanzibaríes, pueblo belicoso, son conocidos en este país sobre todo por un amenazante incidente diplomático ocurrido hace algunos años.
biercEN: An inhabitant of the Sultanate of Zanzibar, off the eastern coast of Africa. The Zanzibaris, a warlike people, are best known in this country through a threatening diplomatic incident that occurred a few years ago. The American consul at the capital occupied a dwelling that faced the sea, with a sandy beach between. Greatly to the scandal of this official's family, and against repeated remonstrances of the official himself, the people of the city persisted in using the beach for bathing. One day a woman came down to the edge of the water and was stooping to remove her attire (a pair of sandals) when the consul, incensed beyond restraint, fired a charge of bird-shot into the most conspicuous part of her person. Unfortunately for the existing entente cordiale between two great nations, she was the Sultana.
revelationES: Zanzibarí es de esas cosas que criticas en otros y justificas en ti mismo.
revelationEN: You search for the meaning of Zanzibari your whole life. Maybe the point is exactly not finding it.

biercES: Cierto trastorno nervioso que aflige a los jóvenes e inexpertos. Pasión que precede a un traspié.
biercEN: A certain nervous disorder afflicting the young and inexperienced. A passion that goeth before a sprawl.
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Celo es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: You assumed Zeal for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: El punto del cielo directamente sobre la cabeza de un hombre de pie, o de un repollo en crecimiento. No se considera que un hombre acostado, o un repollo en la olla, tengan cenit, aunque sobre este punto hubo en su día un considerable disenso entre los eruditos.
biercEN: The point in the heavens directly overhead to a man standing or a growing cabbage. A man in bed or a cabbage in the pot is not considered as having a zenith, though from this view of the matter there was once a considerably dissent among the learned, some holding that the posture of the body was immaterial. These were called Horizontalists, their opponents, Verticalists. The Horizontalist heresy was finally extinguished by Xanobus, the philosopher-king of Abara, a zealous Verticalist. Entering an assembly of philosophers who were debating the matter, he cast a severed human head at the feet of his opponents and asked them to determine its zenith, explaining that its body was hanging by the heels outside. Observing that it was the head of their leader, the Horizontalists hastened to profess themselves converted to whatever opinion the Crown might be pleased to hold, and Horizontalism took its place among fides defuncti.
revelationES: Cenit es exactamente lo que cada quien necesita que sea para tener la razón.
revelationEN: You assumed Zenith for years. You never asked why, until it was already too late.

biercES: Jefe de los dioses griegos, adorado por los romanos como Júpiter y por los americanos modernos como Dios, Oro, Chusma y Perro. Ciertos exploradores que han tocado las costas de América han pensado que estos cuatro nombres representan a cuatro deidades distintas, pero en su obra monumental sobre las Fes Supervivientes, cierto erudito insiste en que los nativos son monoteístas, no teniendo cada uno otro dios que sí mismo, al que adora bajo muchos nombres sagrados.
biercEN: The chief of Grecian gods, adored by the Romans as Jupiter and by the modern Americans as God, Gold, Mob and Dog. Some explorers who have touched upon the shores of America, and one who professes to have penetrated a considerable distance to the interior, have thought that these four names stand for as many distinct deities, but in his monumental work on Surviving Faiths, Frumpp insists that the natives are monotheists, each having no other god than himself, whom he worships under many sacred names.
revelationES: Zeus cambia de significado exactamente cuando te conviene que cambie.
revelationEN: Zeus changes meaning right when it is convenient for it to change.

biercES: Avanzar con incertidumbre, de lado a lado, como quien carga un pesado fardo ajeno.
biercEN: To move forward uncertainly, from side to side, as one carrying the white man's burden. (From zed, z, and jag, an Icelandic word of unknown meaning.)
revelationES: Nadie te lo dice, pero Zigzaguear es solo la forma elegante de aceptar que no hay respuesta.
revelationEN: You name Zigzag and assume you understood it. Naming a thing is not the same as understanding it.

biercES: La ciencia e historia del reino animal, incluyendo a su rey, la Mosca Doméstica. El padre de la Zoología fue Aristóteles, como universalmente se admite, pero el nombre de su madre no ha llegado hasta nosotros.
biercEN: The science and history of the animal kingdom, including its king, the House Fly (Musca maledicta). The father of Zoology was Aristotle, as is universally conceded, but the name of its mother has not come down to us. Two of the science's most illustrious expounders were Buffon and Oliver Goldsmith, from both of whom we learn (L'Histoire generale des animaux and A History of Animated Nature) that the domestic cow sheds its horns every two years.
revelationES: Todos usan Zoología para sonar más inteligentes de lo que la conversación exigía.
revelationEN: Zoology is easy to admire in a book. Uncomfortable to live by in real life.
